title.rendered: Apple Joins China’s Subsidy Program to Boost iPhone, Mac Sales

content.rendered:
In a move to combat declining sales in China, Apple has joined China’s national digital product subsidy program through its direct sales channels, according to the South China Morning Post. This will allow eligible customers in Beijing and Shanghai to receive government-backed discounts on select iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch models.

How the Subsidy Program Works

The program offers a discount of up to 2,000 yuan (approximately $278) on select Apple products, with the device’s price determining eligibility.

Products priced under 6,000 yuan ($835) receive a 15% discount capped at 500 yuan ($70), while higher-value items, like Macs, qualify for larger subsidies.

In Shanghai, customers can benefit from this subsidy by buying an eligible device from one of the eight Apple Stores. Beijing residents, on the other hand, can receive the discount via Apple’s Online Store as long as they use a Beijing shipping address.

First-Time Direct Participation by Apple

This isn’t the first time Apple products have been available under the program. Previously, they were offered only through authorized third-party platforms such as JD.com and Alibaba’s Taobao. However, Apple’s own retail and online stores are now participating directly.

A Response to Declining Shipments

This initiative comes as Apple seeks to revitalize its sales in China, where iPhone sales have declined notably in 2025. Market analysts note that Apple is the only top-five smartphone vendor to see a drop in shipments this year, while rivals like Xiaomi and Huawei have experienced significant growth.

iGeeksBlog Take

As China remains a vital market—and with competitors like Xiaomi and Huawei making aggressive gains—Apple’s direct participation in the program appears both timely and strategic. This can help the Cupertino tech giant reverse its sales slump. Given its premium image, Apple rarely joins such programs, so this is a significant and telling shift in its China strategy.

What’s your take on Apple joining China’s subsidy program? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

excerpt.rendered: Apple has joined China’s national subsidy program for the first time, offering government-backed discounts on iPhones, Macs, and more to combat slowing sales in the region.

title.rendered: Apple Wallet F1 Ad Draws Backlash from iPhone Users

content.rendered:
Apple just pushed the wrong button—literally. This week, the tech giant sent out a push notification through the Wallet app, promoting a $10 Apple Pay discount on two tickets for its upcoming movie F1. What might’ve seemed like harmless marketing to some triggered frustration and distrust among many iPhone users.

A Promo in the Wrong Place?

The notification was part of a partnership with Fandango, offering users a discount when they paid with Apple Pay. On the surface, it’s a harmless promo. However, what caused the stir was where and how Apple chose to deliver it: through the Wallet app, a system-level app that handles sensitive financial tasks, such as storing credit cards, boarding passes, and concert tickets.

For a lot of people, that’s sacred ground. Users took to X, Reddit, and tech forums to air their disappointment. One person posted, “I didn’t drop $1,000+ on an iPhone to get ads from my Wallet app.” Others likened it to a breach of trust, calling it an invasive move that blurs the line between utility and promotion.

Is Apple Breaking Its Own Rules?

It’s not just about discomfort—it might be a direct contradiction of Apple’s own policies. According to Apple’s App Review Guidelines (section 4.5.4), push notifications shouldn’t be used for promotions unless the user explicitly opts in and has an easy opt-out option.

However, in this case, users received the Wallet promo without their consent, and those running iOS 18 found that they couldn’t disable promotions without also shutting off all Wallet notifications. That’s not a viable tradeoff for most.

Interestingly, iOS 26 beta introduces a new toggle in Wallet settings under Notifications labeled “Offers & Promotions.” It allows users to opt out of such promotional content, but this feature is currently only available to developers and beta testers.

The “F1 Push” Is Reminding Users of a Past Mistake

The incident is already drawing comparisons to the infamous U2 album fiasco of 2014, when Apple forced-installed a U2 album onto users’ libraries without consent. That move led to widespread backlash and a rare public apology. Some are now calling this Apple’s “F1 Push” moment of 2025.

Users Divided—But It’s Not Just About $10

Defenders of Apple argue this is overblown. Since Wallet already manages tickets and entertainment, promoting a movie deal might not seem out of place. And hey—$10 off is still a win, right?

However, critics argue that the real concern isn’t the discount, but rather the precedent. If Apple begins treating system apps like marketing channels, what’s next? Ads in Settings? Promos through Health?

It all boils down to trust—something Apple markets heavily with its privacy-first positioning. When a platform like Wallet, built around personal security and discretion, starts pushing ads, it raises red flags for users who expect more from a premium device.

A Slippery Slope for System App Ads?

In an era where digital advertising feels unavoidable, Apple has long stood apart by prioritizing user control and clean, ad-free system experiences. This move signals a shift, and for many, even one push notification was one too many.

If Apple doesn’t course correct, the fear is that this might just be the beginning of a new, more intrusive chapter in how it communicates with users.

title.rendered: Can You See Who Viewed Your Instagram Profile? Find Out Now

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways
  • No. You can’t see who looks at your Instagram profile—no exceptions.
  • You’ll only see who watched your Stories (for 48 hours) or joined your Live video (while it’s happening).
  • Apps that promise to show you profile viewers? They’re scams and can put your account at risk.
  • Instagram gives you privacy tools—use them to control who sees your stuff.
  • If someone makes you uncomfortable, use restrict, block, or report. Instagram keeps these actions private.

You’re not the only one! With so many people using Instagram, it’s totally normal to be curious about who’s visiting your profile. Maybe you’re hoping for a secret admirer, or maybe you just want to know if someone’s “stalking” you. So, does Instagram show who viewed your profile?

Let’s clear up the confusion. This guide breaks down what Instagram actually shows you, what stays private, why those “profile viewer” apps are a bad idea, and how you can stay safe and in control.

Table of Contents
  • Can You See Who Views Your Profile on Instagram
  • What Can You Actually See on Instagram?
  • Instagram vs. Other Social Platforms
  • Why Does Instagram Keep Profile Views Private?
  • What Activity Can You See on Instagram?
  • Instagram Business Accounts and Analytics
    • Instagram Insights lets you track:
    • How to Access Instagram Insights:
    • What Can You See About Post Engagement?
  • Common Myths, Scams, and Misconceptions
  • Third-Party Apps: Risks and Reality
  • How to Protect Your Privacy on Instagram
    • How to block someone:
    • Manage Story and Post Visibility
    • If You Feel Unsafe or Harassed
  • The Role of Instagram's Algorithm
  • Ethical and Social Considerations
  • The Truth About Instagram Profile Views

Can You See Who Views Your Profile on Instagram

Short answer: Nope! Instagram does not let anyone see who’s checked out their profile. This is true for everyone—personal, creator, or business accounts, and on any device. Instagram keeps profile browsing totally anonymous.

For example: LinkedIn sometimes tells you when someone views your profile. Instagram? It never does.

What Can You Actually See on Instagram?

Instagram treats every feature a little differently. Here’s how it works:

  1. Profile: You can’t see who visits, ever.
  2. Stories: You can see who watched your Story, but only for 48 hours after you post it.
  3. Highlights: Once a Story becomes a Highlight, the viewer info disappears.
  4. Reels and Feed Posts: You’ll see who liked, commented, or shared—but not who just viewed.
  5. Profile Picture: No one can see if you viewed their profile photo.
  6. Live Video: If you go live, you’ll see who’s watching in real time, but that list goes away when the live ends.

Instagram vs. Other Social Platforms

How does Instagram’s privacy approach compare to other major social platforms?

Insight: Instagram is stricter than most platforms about profile view privacy, letting users explore content freely without exposing their browsing activity.

Why Does Instagram Keep Profile Views Private?

Instagram’s goal is to let you browse and discover new accounts without feeling watched or judged. Keeping profile views private means you can explore freely—no pressure, no drama.

What Activity Can You See on Instagram?

While profile views are always private, you can see who interacts with your content in specific ways:

Instagram Stories

  1. When you post a Story, you can view a list of who’s watched it by swiping it up while it’s active.
  2. Viewer list is available for up to 48 hours after posting.
  3. The order of viewers is influenced by your interactions and Instagram’s algorithm—it’s not strictly chronological or a sign of “stalking.”

Example: If you post a Story at 10 am, you can check the viewer list until 10 am two days later. After that, the viewer data disappears.

Instagram Business Accounts and Analytics

Business or creator accounts get access to Instagram Insights. While you still can’t see individual profile. viewers, you’ll get useful aggregated data to help grow your presence.

Instagram Insights lets you track:

  1. Profile visits: Total number of times your profile was viewed in a given period.
  2. Follower growth: How many followers you gained or lost over time.
  3. Impressions and reach: How often your content was seen and by how many unique accounts.
  4. Audience demographics: Age, gender, top locations, and when your followers are most active.
  5. Content performance: Engagement metrics for each post, Story, Reel, or Live.
  6. Website and action button clicks: Number of users who clicked your bio link, called, emailed, or requested directions.

How to Access Instagram Insights:

  1. Switch to a Professional Account (Business or Creator) under Settings > Account.
  2. Post content and allow at least 7 days for data to start populating.
  3. Tap “Insights” on your profile or view analytics for individual posts and Stories.

Important: Instagram Insights only shows aggregate numbers and trends. You’ll never see a list of individual profile visitors.

Example: You might learn that your profile had 200 visits last week, but you won’t know who those visitors were.

What Can You See About Post Engagement?

You can always see:

  1. Who liked, commented on, or shared your posts.
  2. Who viewed your Stories (for a limited time).

If someone just looks at your profile or scrolls through your posts without interacting, you won’t be notified or see their username.

Common Myths, Scams, and Misconceptions

You might see lots of “hacks” or myths online about seeing your profile viewers. Here’s what’s really true:

  • “Turning your account public for a day lets you see profile viewers.”
  • False—Instagram never displays profile viewers, regardless of your account type.
  • “Using certain hashtags or third-party apps will show your stalkers.”
  • False—Instagram’s official policy and API make this impossible.
  • “If someone always watches your Stories, they’re stalking your profile.”
  • Not necessarily—Story views only show who watched your Story, not who visited your profile.

Third-Party Apps: Risks and Reality

No app or service can show you who viewed your Instagram profile. Apps that claim to do so are scams and pose serious security risks:

  1. They often require your Instagram login, which can lead to hacking or data theft.
  2. Many install malware or steal personal information.
  3. Using unauthorized apps can result in your account being suspended or banned.

Instagram’s Stance: Instagram’s terms of service prohibit the collection of profile view data by third parties, and the platform actively works to prevent unauthorized data access.

How to Protect Your Privacy on Instagram

Want more privacy or control? Here’s how to manage who sees your content and interacts with you:

Make Your Account Private

  1. Go to your Instagram profile and tap the three lines in the corner.
  2. Select “Settings and privacy”.
  3. Tap “Account privacy”.
  4. Toggle on “Private account”.

Result: Only people you approve as followers can see your posts and Stories.

Restrict or Block Users

  1. Restrict: Limits what a user can see and do on your profile without notifying them.
  2. Block: Prevents the user from entirely seeing your profile, posts, or Stories.

Related: What happens when you restrict someone on Instagram?

How to block someone:

  1. Visit their Instagram profile.
  2. Tap the three dots in the top right.
  3. Select “Block”.

Manage Story and Post Visibility

  1. Hide Stories from specific users.
  2. Create a Close Friends list for more privacy.

Example: If you want only close friends to see certain Stories, add them to your Close Friends list before posting.

If You Feel Unsafe or Harassed

  1. Restrict or block the user to limit their access to your content.
  2. Make your account private so only approved followers see your posts.
  3. Report harassment using Instagram’s reporting tools.

Note: Instagram keeps these actions private, so blocked users are not notified.

The Role of Instagram’s Algorithm

Sometimes, Instagram’s algorithm might put your content on the Explore page or suggest it to new people. That means more profile visits from strangers—but you’ll never know who they are, and neither will anyone else.

Ethical and Social Considerations

If Instagram revealed profile viewers, would you feel comfortable browsing? There’s a balance between transparency and privacy. While some users want more information, others value anonymity and the freedom to explore profiles without judgment. Instagram’s approach is designed to protect both sides.

In some cultures, browsing profiles openly is normal; in others, privacy is highly valued. Instagram’s privacy tools help users tailor their experience to their own comfort level.

The Truth About Instagram Profile Views

Instagram is all about sharing, connecting, and exploring without worrying about who’s watching. Use the privacy tools, stay smart about your information, and enjoy your time on the app!

Do you want to adjust the tone or explore a specific topic? Let me know—I’m here to help!

FAQs

Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

No. Viewing someone’s profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

title.rendered: What stores take Apple Pay? The ultimate guide for 2026

content.rendered:
Apple Pay has quickly become one of the most popular ways to pay—whether you’re grabbing groceries, shopping for clothes, or fueling up your car. But not every store supports this convenient payment method, so it’s important to know where you can use it before you leave home. In this guide, you’ll find everything you need to know about what stores take Apple Pay, how to spot them, and why it’s worth using.

Table of Contents
  • What is Apple Pay and why does it matter?
  • How does Apple Pay work?
  • Apple Pay vs. Other Mobile payment systems
  • How to identify stores that accept Apple Pay
  • Major US retailers that accept Apple Pay
    • Big Box & Department Stores
    • Book Stores
    • Cinemas
    • Fashion and Lifestyle Brands
    • Grocery Stores & Supermarkets
    • Health & Beauty
    • Home Improvement & Furniture Stores
    • Pet Stores
    • Restaurants and Cafés
    • Sporting Goods
    • Toy Stores & Gaming Stores
    • Gas Stations
    • Websites & Apps
    • E-Commerce Platforms
    • Loyalty and Reward Programs
    • Charities
  • Notable stores that do not accept Apple Pay
  • How to use Apple Pay at stores
  • Benefits and Perks of Using Apple Pay

What is Apple Pay and why does it matter?

Apple Pay is a secure, contactless payment method that lets you make purchases in stores, online, and in apps using your iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad, or Mac. With privacy and ease of use at its core, Apple Pay is accepted by a growing number of retailers. Knowing which stores support it can save you time and hassle at checkout.

How does Apple Pay work?

Apple Pay uses NFC (Near-Field Communication) technology—a small chip in your device that securely communicates with payment terminals. Unlike traditional cards, your card and bank details are never shared with the merchant. Instead, Apple Pay dynamically encrypts each transaction by generating a one-time-use number, keeping your real card details private. This makes Apple Pay not only fast and convenient but also highly secure.

Apple Pay also requires authentication (Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode) before a payment is completed, adding another layer of protection against unauthorized use.

Apple Pay vs. Other Mobile payment systems

While Apple Pay is especially popular in the US, other contactless payment apps like Google Pay and Samsung Pay also use NFC technology to process payments. However, Apple Pay is supported by a broader range of retailers in the US, making it a top choice for iPhone users.

How to identify stores that accept Apple Pay

Wondering if a store takes Apple Pay? Here’s how to find out:

  1. Look for the Apple Pay or contactless payment symbol at checkout—these are usually displayed on payment terminals or at the register.

  2. Use Apple Maps:
    • Open Maps on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.
    • Search for your desired store.
    • Tap the store’s name and scroll to the “Good to Know” or “Useful to Know” section.
    • If you see the Apple Pay logo, you’re good to go!

  3. Check the store’s website or app for Apple Pay support (especially for online shopping).
  4. Ask a staff member if you’re unsure.
  5. Look for the universal contactless symbol (four curved lines) at checkout—Apple Pay works wherever you see this symbol, even if the Apple Pay logo isn’t displayed.
Note Store acceptance may vary by country or region, and sometimes even by location within a chain or franchise. For example, some retailers accept Apple Pay in the US but not in other countries, or vice versa.

Major US retailers that accept Apple Pay

Apple Pay is accepted at thousands of locations across the U.S. and beyond. Here’s a categorized, alphabetized list of notable stores that make checking out with your Apple device quick and easy.

Big Box & Department Stores

These large retailers offer a variety of products and make it easy to pay with Apple Pay at checkout, streamlining your shopping experience.

  • Ace Hardware
  • Apple
  • Best Buy
  • Costco (US and Canada; some locations)
  • Family Dollar
  • Office Depot
  • OfficeMax
  • Pep Boys
  • Staples
  • Target

Book Stores

Whether you’re picking up the latest bestseller or a thoughtful gift, many major book retailers now accept Apple Pay for quick, secure payments.

  • Barnes & Noble
  • Books-A-Million
  • Half-Price Books

Cinemas

Enjoy a seamless night out—several cinema chains let you buy tickets and snacks with a simple tap of your Apple device.

  • AMC
  • Regal Cinemas
  • Cinemark Theaters
  • Showcase
  • Alamo Drafthouse Cinemas

Fashion and Lifestyle Brands

From trendy apparel to accessories, fashion retailers widely support Apple Pay, so you can update your wardrobe without reaching for your wallet.

  • Adidas
  • Aeropostale
  • American Eagle Outfitters
  • Anthropologie
  • Banana Republic
  • Bed Bath & Beyond
  • Bloomingdale’s
  • Champs Sports
  • Crate and Barrel
  • Express
  • Foot Locker
  • Forever 21
  • GAP
  • JCPenney
  • J.Crew
  • Kohl’s
  • Levi’s
  • Macy’s
  • Nike
  • Nordstrom
  • Old Navy
  • REI
  • Saks Fifth Avenue
  • Sephora
  • Ulta Beauty
  • Under Armour
  • Urban Outfitters
  • Victoria’s Secret
  • Wayfair

Grocery Stores & Supermarkets

Stock up on groceries and everyday essentials at national and regional supermarkets that accept Apple Pay for safe, contactless checkout.

  • Acme Markets
  • Albertsons
  • ALDI
  • Bashas’
  • BI-LO
  • Cub Foods
  • Costco (US and Canada; some locations)
  • CVS Pharmacy
  • Dan’s Fresh Market
  • Davis Food & Drug
  • Dick’s Fresh Market
  • Duane Reade
  • Farm Fresh Food & Pharmacy
  • FoodMaxx
  • Hannaford
  • Harveys Supermarket
  • Hornbacher’s
  • Hy-Vee
  • Jewel-Osco
  • Lin’s Fresh Market
  • Lucky
  • Meijer
  • Publix
  • Raley’s
  • Rite Aid
  • Save Mart Supermarkets
  • Schnucks
  • Shaws
  • Shop ‘n Save
  • Shoppers Food & Pharmacy
  • Sprouts Farmers Market
  • Star Market
  • Stater Bros
  • SuperValu
  • Trader Joe’s
  • United Supermarkets
  • Vons
  • Walgreens
  • Wegmans
  • Whole Foods Market
  • Winn-Dixie

Health & Beauty

Many health and beauty chains now support Apple Pay, making it easier to purchase cosmetics, personal care items, and wellness products.

  • Aesop
  • Bath & Body Works
  • Bed Bath & Beyond
  • Diptyque
  • Sephora
  • Ulta Beauty

Home Improvement & Furniture Stores

Upgrade your home or workspace with purchases from home improvement and furniture stores that accept Apple Pay for added convenience.

  • Ace Hardware
  • Crate and Barrel
  • IKEA (select locations)

Pet Stores

Whether you’re buying pet food or supplies, leading pet stores let you use Apple Pay for a faster, more convenient shopping trip.

  • Petco
  • PetSmart

Restaurants and Cafés

From fast food to sit-down dining, a wide range of restaurants and cafés accept Apple Pay, making meals and snacks easier to purchase.

  • Au Bon Pain
  • Baskin-Robbins
  • Burger King
  • Chick-fil-A
  • Chili’s
  • Chipotle
  • Domino’s
  • Dunkin’ Donuts
  • El Pollo Loco
  • Firehouse Subs
  • Fuddruckers
  • Jamba Juice
  • Jersey Mike’s Subs
  • Jimmy John’s
  • Johnny Rockets
  • KFC
  • Krispy Kreme
  • Little Caesars
  • McDonald’s
  • Moe’s
  • Panera Bread
  • Pizza Hut
  • Rubio’s
  • Sonic
  • Starbucks
  • Subway
  • Taco Bell
  • Wendy’s
  • White Castle

Sporting Goods

Get your gear and apparel quickly—major sporting goods stores now accept Apple Pay for a swift, secure checkout.

  • Champs Sports
  • Dick’s Sporting Goods
  • REI

Toy Stores & Gaming Stores

Toy and gaming retailers make it easy to buy gifts or the latest releases with Apple Pay, ensuring a smooth shopping experience.

  • Best Buy
  • Disney Stores
  • GameStop
  • Lego
  • Toys R Us (inside select Macy’s)

Gas Stations

Fill up your tank and grab snacks at participating gas stations that support Apple Pay for quick, contactless transactions.

  • 7-Eleven
  • Chevron
  • Circle K
  • Costco (select locations)
  • ExxonMobil (via Speedpass+ app)
  • Red Apple
  • Texaco

Websites & Apps

Many popular websites and mobile apps let you check out with Apple Pay, making online shopping faster and more secure.

  • Airbnb
  • Apple Store
  • Chick-fil-A
  • Chipotle
  • DoorDash
  • Etsy
  • Expedia
  • Fandango
  • Grubhub
  • Instacart
  • Lyft
  • MLB
  • NFL
  • OpenTable
  • Panera Bread
  • Postmates
  • Seamless
  • Starbucks
  • Ticketmaster
  • Uber
  • United Airlines
  • ZARA

E-Commerce Platforms

If you run an online store, major e-commerce platforms support Apple Pay integration, offering your customers a seamless payment option.

  • BigCommerce
  • GoDaddy
  • Salesforce
  • Shopify
  • WooCommerce

Loyalty and Reward Programs

Earn and redeem rewards even faster—several loyalty programs and digital passes now support Apple Pay for effortless points collection.

  • Coca-Cola’s Vending Pass
  • Dave & Buster’s Power Card
  • Jimmy John’s Freaky Fast Rewards
  • Kohl’s Rewards
  • Panera Bread’s MyPanera
  • Walgreens’ Balance Rewards

Charities

Support your favorite causes with ease, as many well-known charities now accept donations through Apple Pay.

  • (RED)
  • American Cancer Society
  • American Red Cross
  • Doctors Without Borders
  • Feeding America
  • UNICEF
  • World Wildlife Fund

Notable stores that do not accept Apple Pay

While Apple Pay is widely accepted, there are some major exceptions. As of 2026, the following stores do not take Apple Pay:

  • Walmart (offers Walmart Pay app as an alternative)
  • Sam’s Club (offers Sam’s Club Scan & Go app)
  • Home Depot (U.S. locations; available in Canada)
  • Kroger (offers Kroger Pay app)
  • Lowe’s
  • Kmart
  • Hobby Lobby
  • Red Lobster
  • Applebee’s
  • Arby’s
  • Boston Market
  • Carl’s Jr
  • Cheesecake Factory
  • Gordon Food Service

Some of these retailers offer their own mobile payment solutions, so you can still use your phone to check out, just not with Apple Pay.

Regional Differences:

Some chains may only accept Apple Pay in certain countries or at select locations. For example, Costco and Home Depot accept Apple Pay in Canada but not all U.S. locations. Always check locally or use Apple Maps to confirm.

How to use Apple Pay at stores

Paying with Apple Pay is simple and secure. Here’s how:

In-Store:

  1. Double-click the side button on your iPhone or Apple Watch.
  2. Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode.
  3. Hold your device near the contactless reader until you see “Done” and a checkmark.

Online or In-App:

  1. Choose Apple Pay at checkout.
  2. Confirm your payment with Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode.

Apple Pay works with most recent iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad, and Mac models.

Tip You can use Apple Pay at many smaller and independent businesses, not just national chains. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, your Apple Pay should work—even if the Apple Pay logo isn’t displayed.

Benefits and Perks of Using Apple Pay

Security: Your card details are never shared with merchants. Apple Pay uses dynamic, one-time-use codes for each transaction, making it extremely difficult for thieves to steal your information.

Privacy: Apple doesn’t track your purchases, and your actual card numbers are not stored on your device or Apple’s servers. Each transaction is kept private between you, the merchant, and your bank.

Convenience: Leave your wallet at home—just tap and go with your iPhone or Apple Watch. Apple Pay works for in-store, online, and in-app purchases, as well as public transit in many cities.

Speed: Payments are processed instantly, whether you’re at the checkout, boarding a train, or sending money to a friend.

Protection: Your device must be unlocked and authenticated (with Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode) before payments can be made. Cards cannot be copied or skimmed like traditional plastic cards, adding an extra layer of safety.

Versatility: Apple Pay supports thousands of banks and credit unions and works seamlessly with a wide range of retailers, apps, and services.

Exclusive Perks:

  • Apple Card Integration: Earn daily cashback rewards on purchases made with Apple Card through Apple Pay, with no fees and enhanced privacy.
  • Apple Cash: Instantly send and receive money with friends and family through Messages, or use your Apple Cash balance for purchases.
  • Loyalty and Rewards: Add loyalty cards and digital passes to the Wallet app and automatically earn or redeem points at checkout—no need to carry extra cards.
  • Transit Access: In many major cities, use Apple Pay to pay for subway, bus, or train fares with a simple tap.
  • Peer-to-Peer Payments: Easily split bills and pay friends directly from your device, making group outings and reimbursements hassle-free.

That’s all for now!

Apple Pay makes shopping easier, faster, and more secure—whether you’re in-store or online. With thousands of retailers now accepting Apple Pay, you can leave your wallet at home and pay with just a tap. Bookmark this guide for future reference, and check back for updates as more stores join the list.

Have questions or know a store that should be added? Drop a comment below!

FAQs

Can I use Apple Pay online?

Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

Which browsers support Apple Pay?

Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

Want to know more about Apple Pay? Check out these articles now:

  • Apple Pay Not Working on iPhone? Here is How to Fix it
  • How to use Tap to Pay on iPhone
  • Apple Pay Keeps Asking to Update Shipping Contact

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

mainEntity.name: Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: Everything New in macOS 26 Beta 2: Features and Changes

content.rendered:
Apple has officially rolled out the second developer beta of macOS 26—also known as macOS Tahoe—alongside iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and watchOS 26 beta 2.

While this update doesn’t introduce sweeping changes, it fine-tunes what was unveiled at WWDC 2025 and subtly prepares the Mac for a smarter, more integrated future. Here’s a complete breakdown of what’s new in macOS 26 Developer Beta 2.

Frosted Menu Bar Background Toggle Returns

In Beta 1, the menu bar remained fully transparent, allowing wallpapers to show through, which often compromised readability.

Beta 2 adds a much-needed toggle under Settings > Menu Bar called “Show menu bar background.” When enabled, it applies a frosted glass blur, making the menu bar feel cohesive with Apple’s new Liquid Glass design while improving visibility.

Classic Finder Icon Restored

Apple sparked a wave of confusion in Beta 1 by flipping the iconic Finder icon’s color scheme for the first time in decades.

In Beta 2, Apple wisely reverts to the familiar blue-left, white-right design, restoring visual consistency and pleasing long-time Mac fans.

Refreshed Migration Assistant Icon

The Migration Assistant app also got a fresh look. Apple has updated its icon to better match the current macOS design language. There are no functionality changes, but the updated icon helps it feel more modern and in line with other system apps.

All-New Recovery Assistant

One of the most important additions in macOS 26 is the Recovery Assistant. If your Mac doesn’t boot normally, this tool automatically diagnoses and attempts to fix issues—no need to enter recovery mode or use Terminal. It’s a game-changer for casual users who may not be comfortable with advanced troubleshooting steps.

Foundation Models Framework for AI-Powered Apps

For developers, macOS 26 now includes the Foundation Models framework. This allows apps to tap into Apple’s on-device large language models (LLMs)—the same ones behind Apple Intelligence.

These models can perform tasks like summarizing text or generating responses without needing an internet connection. Developers can build smarter, AI-powered features while still keeping things private and on-device.

Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the Mac App Store

macOS 26 enhances App Store transparency with Accessibility Nutrition Labels, helping users quickly see which features—like VoiceOver or Dynamic Text—each app supports.

This change empowers users with disabilities to make more informed download decisions.

Linux Container Support Arrives

macOS 26 adds native support for running Linux containers. This is useful for developers, testers, and power users who want to build or deploy Linux-based tools directly on their Mac. It makes workflows simpler and removes the need for third-party virtual machines in many cases.

iMessage and Phone App Improvements

In Beta 2, iMessage gets a useful upgrade that lets you create and vote in polls directly within group chats. This makes it easy to gather opinions or make group decisions without sending multiple messages back and forth.

On the other hand, the Phone app on the Mac becomes more powerful with the addition of Hold Assist. This feature can stay on the line for you during a call and alert you when someone picks up, saving you time. It also introduces Live Translation, allowing you to translate conversations in real time while you’re on a call—perfect for multilingual communication.

Bug Fixes and Visual Tweaks

This beta squashes several bugs and refines the experience:

  • Finder now respects Dark Mode, properly displaying icons and color schemes.
  • Notes and Mail no longer display menu glitches.
  • Messages correctly re-translate edits.
  • Siri’s visual responses no longer get stuck behind translucent UI.
  • Full-screen layout issues in some apps are resolved.
  • Undo stack bugs in TextEditor are fixed.
  • ABC-India keyboard users now see the ₹ symbol by default. The backtick is still available using Option + key.

What’s Next?

Apple hasn’t published a full changelog for Developer Beta 2, but most changes are focused on polish, visual consistency, and backend preparation for public release. The public beta is expected in July, likely with Beta 3 or 4.

macOS 26 isn’t just about flashy features—it’s about slowly shifting how we use the Mac. With tighter iPhone integration, smarter tools, and a final nod to Intel, this beta sets the stage for what the future of macOS looks like.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

mainEntity.name: Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: How to Create a Bootable USB Installer for macOS Tahoe 26

content.rendered:
If you want to try the new macOS Tahoe 26, fix a Mac that’s acting up, or set up multiple Macs, a bootable USB installer is your go-to tool. It offers faster installation, safer beta testing, easy recovery, and offline setup. In this guide, I’ll show you how to create a bootable USB installer for macOS Tahoe 26 in simple, beginner-friendly steps.

Table of Contents
  • Why Do You Need a Bootable USB Installer?
  • What You Need Before You Begin
  • Step-by-Step: Create a macOS Tahoe Bootable USB Installer
    • Step 1: Download macOS Tahoe 26 Installer
    • Step 2: Format the USB Drive
    • Step 3: Use Terminal to Create the Bootable Installer
    • Step 4: Verify the USB Installer
  • Alternate Tools to Create macOS Tahoe USB Installer
  • How to Install macOS Tahoe Using the Bootable USB
    • For Apple Silicon Macs:
    • For Intel Macs (2019–2020):
  • Expert Tips for a Smooth Experience
  • Can't Use the Bootable USB Installer? Here Are the Fixes

    Why Do You Need a Bootable USB Installer?

    A bootable USB installer is a small but powerful tool. Here’s why it’s useful:

    • Perform a clean install to fix persistent bugs or declutter your Mac.
    • Install macOS Tahoe on multiple Macs without re-downloading the ~16GB installer every time.
    • Deploy macOS offline, especially in places with poor or no internet.
    • Recover a non-booting Mac and reinstall the OS quickly.
    • Safely test the macOS Tahoe 26 developer beta on an external drive without affecting your main system.

    What You Need Before You Begin

    Make sure you have the following before starting:

    • Compatible Mac: macOS Tahoe works on all Apple Silicon Macs (M1 and later) and some Intel-based Macs. Check our guide on macOS 26 supported devices to confirm your model. 
    • USB Drive (32GB or more): Use a USB 3.0/USB-C drive for faster performance. Back up its contents—this process erases the drive.
    • macOS Tahoe Installer (Beta): Approximately 16–18GB. You’ll get the download link below.
    • Apple Developer Account: Required to access beta installers.
    • Internet Connection: Needed to download and verify the installer.
    • Time Machine Backup: Always back up your Mac using Time Machine or another tool before installing a new OS, especially a beta version. 
    • Admin Access: You’ll need it to run Terminal commands.

    Step-by-Step: Create a macOS Tahoe Bootable USB Installer

    Follow along, and you’ll have a working USB installer in no time. 

    Step 1: Download macOS Tahoe 26 Installer

    1. Click this link to get the “InstallAssistant.pkg” for macOS Tahoe beta from Apple. 
    2. Once downloaded, go to Finder > Downloads and double-click the zip file.

    3. Click Continue and follow the prompts on the new dialog box. Then, hit Install. 

    4. Finally, click Close to complete the procedure. Your Mac may prompt you to trash the Installer.  
    5. Next, go to the Application folder in Finder and look for the Install macOS Beta.app to ensure a successful installation. 

    Don’t run the installer yet—just keep it in the Applications folder. 

    Pro Tip: Rename the installer to “Tahoe.app” (Control-click > Rename) to make the next steps easier. 

    Step 2: Format the USB Drive

    1. Insert your USB drive into the Mac.
    2. Open Disk Utility (search for it using Spotlight or find it in Applications > Utilities). 
    3. In Disk Utility, find your USB drive in the left sidebar. Select the top-level name (e.g., SanDisk 32GB), not the volume name below it. 
    4. Click Erase at the top and set these options: 
      • Name: Call it “MyVolume” (or any name you like—just remember it for later). 
      • Format: Choose Mac OS Extended (Journaled). 
      • Scheme: Select GUID Partition Map. 
    5. Click Erase to confirm and wait for the process to finish (usually a minute or two). 

    6. Close Disk Utility when done. 

    Your USB drive is now ready for the next step. 

    Step 3: Use Terminal to Create the Bootable Installer

    Now, we’ll use a macOS tool called createinstallmedia to turn your USB drive into a bootable installer. Don’t worry—Terminal is easier than it sounds! 

    1. Open Terminal (search for it with Spotlight or go to Applications > Utilities > Terminal). 
    2. Type this command, replacing “MyVolume” with the name you gave your USB drive. Also, I have renamed my installer to Tahoe.app.
      sudo /Applications/Tahoe.app/Contents/Resources/createinstallmedia --volume /Volumes/MyVolume 
    3. Press return and then type your admin password when asked (you won’t see the password as you type for security reasons). 
    4. Terminal will ask if you’re sure you want to erase the external USB drive. Type “Y” and press return. 
    5. Wait for the process to finish. This can take 5–10 minutes, depending on your USB drive’s speed. You’ll see progress messages like Copying installer files, Making disk bootable, etc. 
    6. When done, Terminal will say: Install media now available at ‘/Volumes/Install macOS Beta’. 

    That’s it! Your USB is now a bootable installer for macOS Tahoe beta. 

    Step 4: Verify the USB Installer

    1. Eject the USB drive (click the eject icon next to it in Finder). 
    2. Plug it back in. It should appear as Install macOS Beta or a similar option. 
    3. Open the USB drive in Finder. You should see a file called Install Tahoe.app (or similar). There are also hidden boot files, but you don’t need to worry about those. 
    4. If the drive’s name or contents look wrong, repeat Steps 2 and 3 to reformat and recreate the installer. 

    Your USB is ready to install macOS Tahoe 26! 

    Alternate Tools to Create macOS Tahoe USB Installer

    If Terminal feels too tricky, try these user-friendly tools: 

    • Donemax Disk Clone for Mac: This app features a straightforward interface for creating installers without requiring any commands. Use the Make Installer option, click Add > macOS Tahoe Beta.app, select your USB drive, and hit Create a macOS installer. It’s great for beginners.
    • For Hackintosh Users: If you’re installing macOS Tahoe on non-Apple hardware, use OpenCore or Clover bootloader. You’ll need extra files (kexts like Lilu.kext and VirtualSMC.kext) for compatibility.  

    These tools can save time, but the Terminal method is free and reliable. Once macOS Tahoe is publicly released in fall 2025, you can download the installer for both beta and stable macOS versions in Terminal itself. 

    How to Install macOS Tahoe Using the Bootable USB

    Ready to install macOS Tahoe 26? Here’s how to use your USB: 

    For Apple Silicon Macs: 

    1. Shut down your Mac. 
    2. Plug in the USB, then press and hold the power button until you see “Loading startup options.” 
    3. Select Install macOS Beta and click Continue. 

    For Intel Macs (2019–2020): 

    1. Shut down your Mac. 
    2. Plug in the USB, then press the power button and immediately press and hold the Option (⌥) key. 
    3. When the boot picker appears, choose Install macOS Beta and press return. 

    Choose Your Install Method:

    • Clean Install: In the macOS Utilities window, open Disk Utility, erase your Mac’s drive (use APFS format and GUID Partition Map), then return to the main menu and select Install macOS. 
    • Upgrade: Select Install macOS to update your current system while keeping files and apps. 
    • Dual-Boot: Create a new APFS volume in Disk Utility and install macOS Tahoe there to keep your existing OS. 

    Finally, follow the prompts to complete the installation. The installer will copy files and restart your Mac a few times. It can take 30–60 minutes, depending on your Mac and USB speed.  

    Your Mac must be connected to a stable Wi-Fi to verify the update with Apple’s servers. After installation, follow the setup wizard to set up your Mac. 

    Expert Tips for a Smooth Experience

    Make your bootable USB experience even smoother with these tips: 

    • Choose a USB 3.0 or 3.1 drive to cut down creation and installation time. Look for brands like SanDisk or Samsung. 
    • Label your USB “Tahoe Installer” or similar to avoid confusion with other drives. 
    • Keep the USB with your Time Machine backup for a complete recovery kit. 
    • macOS Tahoe 26 is in beta, so bugs are possible. Install it on a secondary Mac or partition, not your main work device. 
    • When Apple releases new betas or the final version (expected fall 2025), recreate the USB with the latest installer for the best experience. 

    Can’t Use the Bootable USB Installer? Here Are the Fixes

    Running into problems? Try these solutions: 

    USB Not Showing in Boot Menu: 

    • Open Disk Utility and confirm the USB is formatted as Mac OS Extended (Journaled) with GUID Partition Map. 
    • Try another USB port or a different USB drive. Avoid using hubs or dongles on newer Macs. 
    • For Apple Silicon Macs, boot into Recovery mode (hold power button), open Startup Security Utility, and enable Allow booting from external media. 

    Installer Won’t Create: 

    • Ensure Install macOS Tahoe Beta.app is in the Applications folder, not elsewhere. 
    • Ensure your USB drive has sufficient free space (at least 32GB). 
    • If the installer seems corrupted, re-download it from Apple. 

    Terminal Errors:  

    • Make sure that the Install macOS Beta.app is in the Applications folder. 
    • Use proper backslashes and no spaces in Terminal. 
    • Enter your admin password properly. 
    • To prevent errors, copy and paste the command rather than typing it yourself. 

    Installation Fails: 

    • Verify your Mac supports macOS Tahoe 26. 
    • Ensure a stable internet connection is maintained during the installation process. 
    • In macOS Utilities, use Disk Utility to repair the target drive (select the drive > First Aid). 
    • Re-create the bootable installer on the USB drive. 
    • Ensure your Mac has at least 25–30 GB of free space on the internal drive. 

    USB Creation is Slow:

    • Use a USB 3.0 or USB-C drive for faster performance. 
    • Quit background apps and processes while creating. 
    • If the USB stick continues to stall, reformat it and try again. 

    Still Stuck? Contact Apple Support for detailed troubleshooting. 

    Install macOS Tahoe Quickly with a Bootable USB

    Creating a bootable USB installer for macOS Tahoe 26 is one of the most efficient ways to explore the new OS, recover a bricked Mac, or manage bulk installations. Just follow the steps, back up your data, and you’ll be ready to dive into everything macOS Tahoe has to offer—without the wait.

    Need help or have questions? Drop them in the comments below—we’re happy to assist.

    Want more macOS tips and tricks? Here’s some:

    • How to Format USB Drive on Mac
    • Spotlight in macOS 26 Tahoe: Everything You Can Do With It
    • macOS 26 Tahoe: How to Change Folder Icons Using Emojis, Symbols, or Colors

title.rendered: iOS 26 Beta 2 Hints at New Ultra-Slim iPhone 17 Air Size

content.rendered:
Apple just rolled out the second developer beta of iOS 26, packed with bug fixes and performance improvements. But beyond the usual polish, this update quietly reveals something much bigger—a possible all-new iPhone model. And all signs point to the long-rumored iPhone 17 Air, expected to launch this fall.

Clownfish Wallpaper Reveals a Clue

According to a report by Macworld, Apple included a version of its iconic clownfish wallpaper in the new beta, rendered at 420 x 912 @3x, or 1260 x 2736 pixels. That screen resolution doesn’t match any current iPhone on the market. However, it closely aligns with early leaks surrounding the iPhone 17 Air, which is rumored to introduce a new size to the lineup.

It Matches Kuo’s Prediction—Almost Exactly

Respected Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo previously predicted that the iPhone 17 Air would feature a 6.6-inch display with a resolution of approximately 1260 x 2740. That’s nearly identical to the resolution discovered in iOS 26 Beta 2. It’s a strong indicator that this wallpaper was tailor-made for the ultra-slim device.

Ultra-Slim Design, Big Ambitions

Apple is reportedly planning to discontinue the iPhone Plus model and introduce the iPhone 17 Air in its place. This sleek new phone will slot between the standard iPhone 17 and the iPhone 17 Pro, offering a balanced screen size with a super-thin profile—just 5.5mm thick, according to leaks.

The iPhone Air may also be the first to showcase Apple’s in-house C1 modem, expected to improve connectivity and reduce dependence on Qualcomm. In addition, it could feature a minimalist single-lens rear camera, further reinforcing its slim and lightweight appeal.

The iPhone 17 Air Is Likely Real—And Coming Soon

While whispers of a slim iPhone have circulated for months, this new clue from iOS 26 Beta 2 adds serious credibility. Apple clearly built something to match that screen size. And with the full iPhone 17 lineup expected in September alongside the official iOS 26 release, we won’t have to wait long to find out.

Apple may be ushering in a new era of sleek, thin smartphones with the iPhone 17 Air. If the rumors hold true, this could become the go-to model for users who want style and portability, without sacrificing display size.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: Everything New in iOS 26 Beta 2: Features, Changes & More

content.rendered:
Apple just dropped the second developer beta of iOS 26, and while it doesn’t bring dramatic overhauls, it refines almost every corner of what Beta 1 introduced. From interface tweaks to new Apple Music tricks and improved system features, iOS 26 Beta 2 is shaping up to be a polished and performance-ready update. Here’s everything you need to know.

Table of Contents
  • Liquid Glass Gets a Much-Needed Upgrade
  • Control Center: Darker, Sharper, Better
  • New Ringtone: A Twist on the Familiar
  • Visual Polish and UI Fixes
  • iMessage and Phone App Improvements
  • Apple Music Just Got Smarter
  • Safari: A Tweak for Better Usability
  • New Alert Badges
  • Journaling and Wallet: Real Functionality Boosts
  • Accessibility Highlights in App Store
  • Recovery Assistant Improvements
  • Bug Fixes and Stability Improvements
  • iOS 26 Beta 2 Polishes the Experience

Liquid Glass Gets a Much-Needed Upgrade

The flashy new Liquid Glass UI introduced in Beta 1 looked great on paper, but had some real usability issues, particularly with visibility. The translucent backgrounds made it tough to see buttons and text.

With Beta 2, Apple is fixing that. The Control Center now has a stronger blur effect, improving clarity around sliders and toggles. Notifications also show better contrast, though they can still struggle a bit on very bright wallpapers.

Control Center: Darker, Sharper, Better

Beyond the blur boost, the Control Center now appears slightly darker and more defined. The difference is subtle, but it helps make controls easier to spot and tap quickly.

New Ringtone: A Twist on the Familiar

There’s a new remix of the familiar “Reflection” ringtone, dubbed “Alt 1.” You’ll find it under Settings > Sounds & Haptics > Ringtone. It keeps the same melody but adds a more glassy spin—something that goes well with the new Liquid Glass design on iOS 26.

Visual Polish and UI Fixes

Apple has reintroduced model-specific iPhone wallpapers that were previously missing in Beta 1. Lock Screen layout bugs have been ironed out, too—Focus Mode text no longer clashes with widgets.

Across the system, several icons and UI elements now feature a shinier, more glass-like finish to better match the new design language.

iMessage and Phone App Improvements

iMessage now lets you create polls in chats, including group chats—a helpful addition to the chat backgrounds feature from Beta 1.

On the Phone side, Hold Assist listens while you’re on hold and pings you when a real person joins. Spam detection is also better, making unwanted calls easier to block or silence.

Apple Music Just Got Smarter

Beta 2 brings some notable upgrades to Apple Music. AutoMix creates seamless transitions between songs, while Lyrics Translation helps you follow tracks in other languages. Lyrics Pronunciation is also new, helping you sing along more accurately. Plus, you can now auto-pin favorite songs and use a Live Radio widget for instant access to stations.

Safari: A Tweak for Better Usability

The Safari browser got a subtle redesign. The “More” menu (shown by the three-dot icon) now opens into a single-column list, making options easier to scroll through. Some other layout elements in tab view have also been adjusted slightly.

New Alert Badges

Messages from unknown senders now display a blue alert badge instead of a red one. This makes them feel less alarming and easier to spot without looking like a warning.

Journaling and Wallet: Real Functionality Boosts

On iPads, the Journaling app now supports iCloud sync—a long-requested feature. Apple Wallet also received a significant upgrade: you can now track your online orders inside the app. If you paid with Apple Pay or a supported app, Wallet shows the delivery status, tracking number, and expected arrival—all in one place. This makes it easier to manage your purchases without switching between email and courier apps.

Accessibility Highlights in App Store

A new section on App Store product pages now highlight each app’s Accessibility features—like VoiceOver support, larger text options, or compatibility with AssistiveTouch. This helps users quickly identify which apps are more accessible for individuals with vision, mobility, or hearing challenges.

Recovery Assistant Improvements

Apple redesigned Recovery Mode in iOS 26. Instead of a simple image, you now get on-screen instructions and tools. The new Recovery Assistant can even help restore your iPhone using another iOS device or iPad without requiring a Mac or PC.

Bug Fixes and Stability Improvements

This update fixes the broken AutoMix feature in AirPlay and improves text visibility in the Apple TV app. Overall system performance is more stable, although bugs are still expected at this early stage of the beta cycle.

iOS 26 Beta 2 Polishes the Experience

Overall, iOS 26 Beta 2 feels like a step in the right direction. Apple is clearly listening to feedback and refining both form and function. A public beta lands in July, with the final release expected this fall.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

mainEntity.name: Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: Why Is One AirPod Louder Than the Other? 10 Fixes for Perfect Balance

content.rendered:
Ever noticed one AirPod sounding louder than the other, ruining your music or podcast experience? This frustrating imbalance can stem from dirt buildup, misconfigured settings, or even hardware issues. In this guide, I’ll explain why it happens and walk you through 10 tried-and-tested solutions to restore perfect audio balance in your AirPods.

Table of Contents
  • Why Is One AirPod Louder Than the Other?
  • Clean Your AirPods and Charging Case
  • Reset Audio Balance and EQ Settings
  • Ensure Both AirPods Are Fully Charged
  • Turn Off Head-Tracked Spatial Audio
  • Re-Pair Your AirPods
  • Restart Your iPhone or iPad
  • Update AirPods Firmware
  • Test Fit and Try Another Device
  • Reset Your AirPods to Factory Settings
  • Use Mono Audio (Temporary Fix)
  • When to Consider Replacing Your AirPods
  • How to Prevent the Issue in the Future
  • Fixed: One AirPod Louder Than the Other

Why Is One AirPod Louder Than the Other?

Uneven audio in AirPods can happen for several reasons.  

  • Dirt or earwax might clog the speaker mesh, muffling sound.  
  • Sound settings, such as audio balance or equalizer adjustments, may be misconfigured.  
  • Battery issues, improper fit, or outdated firmware can also cause one AirPod to sound quieter.  
  • In rare cases, hardware damage might be the culprit. 

The good news? Most of these issues can be resolved with simple troubleshooting. Let’s dive into the fixes.

1. Clean Your AirPods and Charging Case

A dirty speaker mesh is one of the most common reasons for uneven sound.

Here’s how to clean your AirPods:

  • Gently wipe the AirPods with a dry, lint-free cloth to remove surface dust. 
  • Use a small brush to clear debris from the speaker mesh. Be gentle to avoid pushing dirt deeper. 
  • Dampen a cotton swab with isopropyl alcohol (don’t soak it) and clean the mesh and crevices. 
  • For the charging case, clean the charging ports with a dry brush or toothpick to remove debris. 
  • Let everything dry completely before testing the audio. 
Tip Avoid water and sharp objects. If you have AirPods Pro, remove and clean the silicone ear tips separately.

2. Reset Audio Balance and EQ Settings

Sometimes your iPhone or iPad’s audio settings are to blame.

Steps to reset audio balance:

  1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Audio & Visual. 
  2. Find the Balance slider (L-R). Ensure it’s centered. If it’s tilted left or right, adjust it to the middle. 

  3. Then, go back and tap on Apps. Select Music > EQ and select Flat or Off to avoid boosting one side. 3

This resets any software-based sound imbalance.

3. Ensure Both AirPods Are Fully Charged

One AirPod with a lower battery may sound quieter or disconnect intermittently.

How to check battery levels:

  1. Place both AirPods in their case, open the lid, and hold them near your iPhone.
  2. Take one AirPod out of the case. A pop-up will show the battery levels for each AirPod and the case.

     
  3. If you see a low battery, charge it for at least 15–20 minutes using a Lightning or USB-C cable (depending on your model).  

4. Turn Off Head-Tracked Spatial Audio

Personalized Spatial Audio (available on AirPods Pro and AirPods Max) adjusts sound based on head movement, which can sometimes make one AirPod seem louder.

To disable it: 

  1. On your iPhone/iPad, open Settings and select your AirPods. 
  2. Tap on Personalised Spatial Audio and select Stop Using Personalised Spatial Audio.

Alternative: Open the Control Center, press and hold the volume slider, and turn off Spatial Audio. 

5. Re-Pair Your AirPods

Reconnecting your AirPods from scratch can resolve connection glitches that cause uneven sound.

Steps to re-pair:

  1. Place both AirPods in their case and close the lid. 
  2. On your device, go to Settings > Bluetooth and tap the (i) button next to your AirPods, then select Forget This Device. 

  3. Open the AirPods case lid, press and hold the setup button on the back until the status light flashes white. 
  4. Reconnect by holding the case near your device and following the on-screen pairing instructions. 

6. Restart Your iPhone or iPad

Sometimes, your device—not the AirPods—is the problem. A restart can fix temporary software issues.

To restart:

  • Press and hold the Side button + volume button until the “slide to power off” appears. Slide to shut down, then turn it back on. 

7. Update AirPods Firmware

Apple releases firmware updates to fix bugs and improve performance.

How to update AirPods firmware:

  1. Put AirPods inside their case and plug the case into a charger. 
  2. Now, place it close to your paired internet-enabled device.
  3. Leave it for 30–60 minutes. Updates install automatically in the background.

8. Test Fit and Try Another Device

A poor fit can affect perceived volume. Plus, testing on another device helps isolate whether the issue lies with the AirPods or your phone.

To test the fit:

  • For AirPods Pro, ensure you’re using the right ear tip size. Go to Settings > Bluetooth > AirPods Pro > Ear Tip Fit Test to check. 
  • Adjust the AirPods to sit snugly in your ears. For AirPods Max, ensure the headband and ear cushions are properly aligned. 
  • Clean your ears gently to ensure no earwax is blocking sound. 

To test another device:

  • Pair your AirPods with another phone, tablet, or computer (e.g., iPad or Mac). 
  • Play audio to see if the volume imbalance persists. If it’s gone, the issue lies with your original device’s settings. 

9. Reset Your AirPods to Factory Settings

When all else fails, a factory reset wipes all settings and connection history to fix stubborn bugs.

To reset:

  1. Place both AirPods in their case and close the lid. 
  2. Wait 30 seconds, then open the lid. 
  3. Press and hold the setup button on the case for 15 seconds until the status light flashes amber, then white. 
  4. Re-pair your AirPods with your device (see step 5). 

If you have AirPods 4 or AirPods Max, follow our guide to reset them quickly. 

10. Use Mono Audio (Temporary Fix)

Until the issue is fully resolved, Mono Audio sends identical sound to both AirPods, bypassing stereo channels.

To enable:

  1. Go to Settings > Accessibility and select Audio & Visual. 
  2. Scroll down and toggle on Mono Audio. 

While it doesn’t fix the root problem, it equalizes audio output for a better experience.

When to Consider Replacing Your AirPods

If none of the solutions fix the issue, it might be time to consider hardware replacement.

Here’s when to replace:

  • Persistent imbalance after trying all fixes
  • Visible damage or water exposure
  • Out-of-warranty devices with known issues

Apple Support Tip: If you’re covered by AppleCare+, you might be eligible for a discounted or free replacement. Standard replacement costs range from $69 to $89 per AirPod, depending on the model.

How to Prevent the Issue in the Future

Prevent uneven sound with regular care:

  • Clean your AirPods and case every 1–2 weeks to prevent buildup. 
  • Keep AirPods in their case when not in use to avoid debris or damage. 
  • Monitor battery levels and avoid letting AirPods fully discharge. 
  • Keep your AirPods and devices updated with the latest software. 
  • For AirPods Pro, use the correct ear tip size for optimal sound. 
  • Don’t expose AirPods to excessive heat, cold, or moisture. 

Fixed: One AirPod Louder Than the Other

A louder AirPod can be annoying, but in most cases, it’s a fixable issue. From simple cleaning and setting tweaks to firmware updates and resets, the steps above will help you restore balanced, crystal-clear sound.

Still stuck? Don’t hesitate to reach out to Apple Support or visit your nearest Apple Store for expert help.

Check out these helpful guides too:

  • iOS 26 Supercharges Your AirPods With These New Features
  • How to Tell If AirPods Are Fake
  • Are AirPods waterproof? Here’s what you need to know

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

title.rendered: watchOS 26 Brings Apple Intelligence to Your Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Apple’s watchOS 26, unveiled at WWDC 2025, introduces a wave of Apple Intelligence features designed to transform your Apple Watch into a more powerful personal assistant. Alongside a refreshed Liquid Glass design, the update introduces AI-driven tools, including a smart workout coach, real-time translations, and context-aware actions, making your wearable even more useful in daily life.

Here’s everything you need to know about the new smart features in watchOS 26.

Table of Contents
  • Which Apple Watch Models Support Apple Intelligence?
  • All the New Apple Intelligence Features in watchOS 26
    • Workout Buddy: Your Personal AI Fitness Coach
    • Live Translation: Break Language Barriers
    • Send Genmoji: Custom Emojis with Personality
    • Smart Actions in Messages: Context-Aware Replies
    • Smart Stack Gets Smarter
    • Smart Call Management: AI Handles the Interruptions
    • Smarter Notifications: Sound That Adapts
  • Apple Intelligence: Now on Your Wrist

Which Apple Watch Models Support Apple Intelligence?

Not all Apple Watches will support the full Apple Intelligence suite. These features rely on advanced hardware, so compatibility is limited to:

  • Apple Watch Series 6 and later
  • Apple Watch SE (2nd generation)
  • Apple Watch Ultra and Ultra 2

Important:

To use Apple Intelligence, your watch must be paired with one of the following iPhones running iOS 26:

  • iPhone 15 Pro or 15 Pro Max
  • Any iPhone 16 model

Older iPhones, even if compatible with iOS 26, won’t enable these advanced AI features.

All the New Apple Intelligence Features in watchOS 26

watchOS 26 is a major upgrade that makes your Apple Watch smarter and more intuitive. Here are all the Apple Intelligence features coming to it.

1. Workout Buddy: Your Personal AI Fitness Coach

One of the most impressive additions is Workout Buddy, an AI-powered fitness coach built into your Apple Watch. It uses data like heart rate, distance, and workout history to give you real-time encouragement and personalized feedback.

For example, it might notify you that you’re nearing a 500-mile milestone or encourage you as you close your Activity Rings. Voice feedback works via Bluetooth headphones, making it feel like a personal trainer is right there with you.

Supported Workouts: Outdoor/Indoor Run and Walk, Outdoor Cycle, HIIT, Functional and Traditional Strength Training.

2. Live Translation: Break Language Barriers

With watchOS 26, your Apple Watch becomes a language translator right on your wrist with the Live Translation feature in the Messages app.  

It translates conversations into your preferred language in real-time, allowing you to easily communicate with people who speak different languages. Moreover, when you reply, your message is translated into the recipient’s language as well.  

Languages at launch: English (US, UK), French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish (Spain), and Chinese (Simplified). More languages, such as Dutch, Danish, and Vietnamese, are expected to be added by the end of 2025.

3. Send Genmoji: Custom Emojis with Personality

You can now send Genmoji—custom AI-generated emojis created on your iPhone—directly from your Apple Watch. Once you create a Genmoji, it syncs to your Apple Watch via iCloud, appearing in the Messages app’s emoji picker. You can tap to send them, just like regular emojis. 

Apple also upgraded Genmoji with iOS 26 by combining emojis, typing a description, or blending two emojis to make a unique one. Therefore, this feature lets you make conversations more expressive. 

4. Smart Actions in Messages: Context-Aware Replies

 

The Messages app in watchOS 26 becomes much smarter, thanks to on-device machine learning. It suggests actions based on message context, like offering to share your location when someone texts, “Are you home yet?”

It even helps in group chats. For instance, if someone sends you a dinner bill, your watch might prompt you to pay them via Apple Cash with one tap.

5. Smart Stack Gets Smarter

Smart Stack now learns from your routine. If you usually start a Pilates workout on Tuesdays at the gym, it may proactively show the workout card when you arrive. Alternatively, if you’re in an area with no signal, consider launching the Backtrack feature.

This widget stack evolves with you, predicting what you need before you even ask.

6. Smart Call Management: AI Handles the Interruptions

watchOS 26 brings Hold Assist and Call Screening directly to your wrist, so you can manage calls hands-free.

  • Hold Assist: If you’re on hold waiting for a live agent, Hold Assist recognizes when the agent is ready and notifies you to return to the call. This means you can put your watch down and focus on something else without missing the moment the agent picks up. 
  • Call Screening: For unknown callers, Call Screening automatically answers the call and asks the caller to state their name and reason for calling. Your watch then alerts you with the details, so you can decide whether to take the call or decline it. 

7. Smarter Notifications: Sound That Adapts

Your Apple Watch now adjusts the notification sound based on your environment. In quiet rooms, it reduces volume to avoid startling you. In louder areas, it boosts alerts so you never miss a ping.

This smart adjustment is made possible by the Apple Watch’s onboard ambient noise detection.

Apple Intelligence: Now on Your Wrist

watchOS 26 is more than just a cosmetic upgrade. It brings meaningful Apple Intelligence features that enhance your everyday life—from staying motivated to bridging language gaps and handling calls smarter than ever.

Which feature are you most excited to try? Let us know in the comments!

Related articles worth reading:

  • watchOS 26 vs watchOS 11: Is Apple’s Latest Update Really Worth It?
  • watchOS 26 Brings Notes to Apple Watch: Here’s How to Use It Like a Pro
  • watchOS 26: How to Use New Wrist Flick Gesture on Apple Watch

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

mainEntity.name: Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.
