title.rendered: 50 Stunning 4K Dynamic Island Wallpapers for iPhone

content.rendered:
If you own an iPhone 16, 15, or 14 Pro, you’re already familiar with the innovative Dynamic Island feature—a clever evolution of the classic notch. But did you know that the right wallpaper can transform your Dynamic Island from a simple cutout into a creative centerpiece? Whether you want to highlight, hide, or playfully incorporate Dynamic Island, the right wallpaper makes all the difference.

In this article, you’ll discover everything you need to know about Dynamic Island wallpapers: what they are, why they matter, how to set them up, and—of course—a handpicked collection of the best HD and 4K options for every style

What Is a Dynamic Island Wallpaper?

Dynamic Island wallpapers are specially designed backgrounds that creatively integrate with the pill-shaped cutout at the top of your iPhone 14 Pro, 15, or 16 display. These wallpapers can:

  • Seamlessly blend the Dynamic Island into the background for a minimalist look.
  • Use playful or artistic elements (like cartoon characters or objects) that interact with the Island.
  • Highlight the notch with gradients, shadows, or bold colors.

The result? Your iPhone’s screen feels more dynamic, personalized, and visually appealing.

Tips for Choosing the Perfect Dynamic Island Wallpaper

  • Personalization: Make your device truly yours by choosing a wallpaper that matches your mood or interests.
  • Creativity: Turn a functional cutout into a fun design element—think cartoon characters hanging from the Island or abstract art that draws the eye.
  • Aesthetic Harmony: Some wallpapers fade or mask the Dynamic Island, making your screen appear sleeker and more unified.
  • Seasonal and Thematic Options: From festive holiday scenes to nostalgic game references, there’s a Dynamic Island wallpaper for every occasion.
  • Consider App Layouts: Some designs work better with certain app arrangements. Minimalist wallpapers often complement busy Home Screens.
  • Try Dark Mode: Wallpapers with dark backgrounds can help the Dynamic Island blend in, especially at night.
Note: Tap the Download button below each wallpaper to save these stunning visuals directly to your iPhone

Best Dynamic Island Wallpapers by Category

Table of Contents
  • 1. Cute & Whimsical Dynamic Island Wallpapers
    • 2. Pop Culture & Cartoons Dynamic Island Wallpapers
      • 3. Superhero Dynamic Island Wallpapers
        • 4. Artistic & Abstract Dynamic Island Wallpapers
          • 5. Nature & Scenery Dynamic Island Wallpapers
            • 6. Nostalgic & Retro Dynamic Island Wallpapers
              • 7. Fun & Playful Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                1. Cute & Whimsical Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Playful, charming designs featuring adorable characters and lighthearted scenes that bring a smile to your iPhone screen.

                Cute Bear

                Add a touch of charm and whimsy as a cute bear peeks out from behind the Dynamic Island on your iPhone. Embrace the magic of this wallpaper and add an extra layer of enchantment to your device.

                Download

                Snoopy Painting

                This wallpaper features Snoopy standing on a red ladder. The background is bright green, making the image pop. Snoopy is holding a paint roller and appears to be painting your Dynamic Island.

                Download

                Minions Antics

                Another fun Minions wallpaper from the Despicable Me movies. It looks like one minion is holding onto the Dynamic Island on your iPhone. Three Minions are standing at the bottom, looking up with fun expressions. Overall, it creates a fun and playful scene on your screen.

                Download

                Minions Fun

                This Minion-themed Dynamic Island wallpaper will give you a heavy dose of fun every time you unlock your iPhone. Tap the download button to watch these lovable characters bring life to your device with their antics.

                Download

                Cute Cat

                This adorable cat-themed Dynamic Island wallpaper is a must-have for all feline enthusiasts. Tap the download button to add a cute, furry companion to your screen and brighten your day.

                Download

                Cats and Mouse

                We don’t want to play a cat-and-mouse game with you. All we want to do is share this cat-and-mouse wallpaper with you.

                Download

                Scrat from the Ice Age

                Why not bring some chaos to your iPhone? Here’s Scrat, the iconic squirrel from Ice Age, hanging from your iPhone’s Dynamic Island! A must-have for Ice Age fans and anyone looking for a fun wallpaper!

                Download

                Shinchan

                Watching Shinchan was and still is an emotional experience! To keep it up, you can download this Shinchan wallpaper that uses Dynamic Island creatively.

                Download

                Wreck-it Ralph

                This vibrant iPhone wallpaper showcases Ralph, the iconic character from Ralph Breaks the Internet, in his signature red plaid shirt and overalls. Perfect for fans of the animated classic, this wallpaper combines playful energy with a modern design.

                Download

                2. Pop Culture & Cartoons Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Wallpapers inspired by iconic movies, TV shows, and beloved cartoon characters—perfect for fans who want to showcase their favorites.

                The Incredibles

                Let’s have some family fun with this black wallpaper for your iPhone inspired from Incredibles movies. A large red spotlight shining down from the top creates a dramatic effect. Download this wallpaper and let the Incredible Family pop up on your iPhone display.

                Download

                Classic Muppets (Bert)

                Do you also love the classic Muppets from Sesame Street? Download this wallpaper featuring Bert with his mad expression. The fun part is his iconic straight eyebrows will replace your Dynamic Island, making your iPhone Lock Screen unique.

                Download

                Simpson’s Burger Catch

                This Dynamic Island wallpaper features playful Simpson reaching up with his mouth wide open, ready to catch a large burger falling towards him. The contrasting backdrop indeed catches the eye. This fun wallpaper is perfect for adding a touch of humor to your iPhone’s screen.

                Download

                Doraemon

                Let’s get back childhood nostalgia with this cute Doraemon wallpaper for your iPhone Dynamic Island. The red vibrant wallpaper with the cartoon logo looks beautiful. Tap the download button to adorn it on your Home Screen.

                Download

                Rick and Morty

                Add a splash of humor to your iPhone with this quirky Rick and Morty wallpaper. It features everyone’s favorite mad scientist with his signature drool and unimpressed gaze. I like how the design blends the notch into his eyebrow. Hilarious!

                Download

                Mario Victory

                Who has not played the classic Super Mario game? Get that nostalgia on your iPhone Home Screen with this Mario Dynamic Island wallpaper. It’s that iconic victory scene from the game we all wanted to achieve!

                Download

                Squid Game

                Squid Game has become another name of thrill and adventure. As season 2 has arrived, deck your iPhone with this Squid Game-inspired wallpaper. Featuring iconic geometric design, this wallpaper makes your Dynamic Island stand out!

                Download

                Dragon Ball Z

                Channel your inner Saiyan with this pixelated Dragon Ball Z wallpaper for Dynamic Island. Watch as your favorite characters come alive on your screen in pixel-perfect glory.

                Download

                Star Trek

                Embark on a course for the stars with this captivating Star Trek-themed Dynamic Island wallpaper. Explore the dynamic voyage of the USS Enterprise on your screen.

                Download

                3. Superhero Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Spider-Man Upside Down

                The Spider-Man wallpaper for iPhone is sure to serve some quirks on a regular, busy day. While I don’t want you to hang upside down, you can definitely let your Marvel superhero do it from the Dynamic Island.

                Download

                Spider-Man Swinging

                Enjoy this cool Dynamic Island wallpaper featuring your friendly neighborhood superhero, Spider-Man. Feel the thrill on your iPhone screen as Miles Morales swings through Queens, New York.

                Download

                Superman

                This one is my personal favorite! If you are also a Marvel fan, you will love this cool Superman wallpaper. The animated look with the vibrant color coming down from the Dynamic Island makes your iPhone one of a kind.

                Download

                Batman Dark and Eerie

                Dive into the mysterious world of Batman with this Batman iPhone wallpaper. With a simple tap on the download button, you can capture the dark and eerie air of Gotham City.

title.rendered: What Is Metal 4 and How It Could Finally Make Mac Gaming Better

content.rendered:
Gaming on a Mac has always been more of a hopeful promise than a reality. Apple has made progress with Apple Silicon, but even today, AAA titles barely trickle in. Now, Apple is trying again, this time with Metal 4, a big upgrade to the technology that powers graphics on the Mac. It was announced at WWDC 2025 and brings real changes that could finally give gaming on Mac a chance.

So if you’re wondering what Metal 4 is, what’s new in this update, and how it could improve gaming on your macOS device, let’s dive in.

Table of Contents
  • What Exactly Is Metal 4?
  • MetalFX: Upscaling, Frame Interpolation, and Denoising
  • Built-in AI Support: Smarter Graphics
  • Games Load Faster and Crash Less
  • Bigger Worlds and Better Effects
  • Easier Porting of Windows Games to Mac
  • Real Games Already Using Metal 4
  • What Devices Support Metal 4?
  • Final Thoughts: Is Metal 4 a Game Changer?

What Exactly Is Metal 4?

Metal 4 is the system that helps your Mac draw everything you see in a game—graphics, lighting, effects, and more. It lets developers work more closely with the hardware, especially Apple Silicon, so games can run faster and look better.

This new version focuses on three big things:

  • Making games smoother and more efficient
  • Allowing developers to use AI directly in games
  • Helping more Windows games come to Mac easily

Now, let’s look at what that means for you.

1. MetalFX: Upscaling, Frame Interpolation, and Denoising

Apple’s MetalFX technology originally focused on upscaling—a method where games are rendered in a lower resolution and then intelligently upscaled to look high-quality. This saves GPU power while still delivering great visuals.

Now, with Metal 4, MetalFX has gotten two powerful upgrades:

  • Frame Interpolation: Instead of rendering every frame from scratch, MetalFX now creates extra frames between two rendered frames. This boosts frame rates without significantly increasing the system’s load. It helps games feel smoother, especially on lower-end Apple devices.
  • Denoising: Games that utilize advanced lighting effects, such as ray tracing, often appear noisy or pixelated when performance is low. Denoising cleans it up, so you still get high-quality lighting and reflections without slowdowns.

Together with upscaling, these features help developers deliver smoother and sharper gameplay while maintaining optimal performance.

2. Built-in AI Support: Smarter Graphics

Here’s where Metal 4 becomes smarter. It lets developers add AI effects directly into games. That means:

  • Lighting in a game can automatically adjust to what’s happening.
  • AI filters can be added in real-time.
  • Games could react to your actions in more intelligent ways.

This type of smart processing used to require separate systems, but now it can run directly on your Mac’s graphics chip alongside game processing.

3. Games Load Faster and Crash Less

Metal 4 enhances the preparation and loading of games. Developers can now reuse parts of code, manage performance better, and avoid wasting time on shader compilation (the stuff that tells your GPU how to draw things).

In short, your games should open faster, feel more stable, and have fewer glitches.

4. Bigger Worlds and Better Effects

Metal 4 also helps games manage memory more wisely. This means:

  • Developers can create bigger game worlds without slowing everything down.
  • Effects like reflections or shadows can look better and still run smoothly.

5. Easier Porting of Windows Games to Mac

Apple also updated its Game Porting Toolkit, which helps developers bring PC games to macOS. Now they can:

  • Build and test Mac games using Windows tools
  • Convert graphics code more easily
  • Use the latest Metal features like upscaling and denoising

This means more games might actually come to Mac and run well.

Real Games Already Using Metal 4

Apple teased that upcoming games, such as Crimson Desert and InZOI, are using MetalFX for smoother performance. Meanwhile, big-name titles like Cyberpunk 2077, Lies of P, and HITMAN are finally making their way to macOS.

Plus, there’s a new Games app launching on Mac, iPhone, and iPad later this year.

What Devices Support Metal 4?

Metal 4 runs on:

  • Macs with Apple Silicon (M1 and later)
  • iPhones and iPads with A14 Bionic and later

Older Intel Macs and iPhones with A13 Bionic or earlier won’t support these features.

Final Thoughts: Is Metal 4 a Game Changer?

Metal 4 might not turn your MacBook Air into a gaming beast overnight. But it’s a clear signal from Apple: they’re serious about gaming. And this time, they’re giving developers actual tools to make it happen.

If more studios embrace Metal 4, and if Apple keeps pushing game development support, Macs might finally get the gaming future they were promised a decade ago.

  • How to Play Windows Games on Mac
  • How to Check FPS in Games on Mac
  • Play Fortnite on Mac: 2025 Step-by-Step Guide

title.rendered: iOS 26 vs Android 16: Form Over Functionality

content.rendered:
Normally, when Apple and Google release new versions of their operating systems, the buzz is all about new features, who copied whom, and what AI trickery is packed in. However, with iOS 26 and Android 16, all eyes are on the looks and aesthetics. From iOS’s glass-like layers to Android’s expressive colors, 2025 is shaping up to be the year where design takes the front seat.

And while both platforms have added some practical features here and there, the headline feature on both platforms this year revolves around design.

Table of Contents
  • iOS 26 vs Android 16: Feature Comparison (Design Aside)
    • What's New on iOS 26?
    • What's New in Android 16?
  • Design Spotlight: Liquid Glass vs Material 3 Expressive
    • iOS 26: Liquid Glass
    • Android 16: Material 3 Expressive
  • Real Talk: Our Take on the New Designs
  • Final Thoughts: 2025 Is the Year of Form Over Function

iOS 26 vs Android 16: Feature Comparison (Design Aside)

Before diving into the visual changes, let’s take a moment to compare the actual features these updates bring to the table.

What’s New on iOS 26?

Apple has finally introduced some features that Android users have had for years:

  • Call Screening: It picks up unknown calls automatically, asks who’s calling and why, and then shows you a transcript so you can decide whether to answer. Pixel phones have been doing this since 2018.
  • Hold Assist: Your iPhone now waits on hold for you and sends a notification when a real person joins the call. It works just like Google’s Hold for Me on Pixel phones.
  • Visual Intelligence: Building on last year’s update, Visual Intelligence now works with what’s on your screen, too. It’s Apple’s take on Google’s Circle to Search feature.
  • Visited Places: Tracks the places you’ve been and organizes them inside Apple Maps—similar to Google Maps Timeline, but more focused on location highlights.
  • Messages Updates: You can personalize chats with custom backgrounds, run polls in group messages, and send or receive Apple Cash within conversations.
  • Apple Intelligence: Adds AI upgrades to Image Playground, Genmoji, and Live Translate. Most of the features are already possible on Android with the help of Gemini.

For more details, check out our detailed guide on iOS 26 features.

What’s New in Android 16?

On the other hand, while Android is bringing new features, most of them are niche and may only be useful for power users:

  • Desktop Windowing: Lets you run multiple apps in resizable windows on large screens like tablets or foldables, just like a desktop setup.
  • Custom Keyboard Shortcuts: Set up personalized keyboard commands to launch apps or perform actions—great for productivity on tablets.
  • Advanced Protection: A new all-in-one security hub that helps you stay protected from scam calls, risky apps, and account takeovers with a single tap.
  • Auto-Grouped Notifications: Automatically bundles similar alerts to reduce clutter and make it easier to focus on what matters.
  • Predictive Back Gesture: Shows a preview of your previous screen before you swipe back, giving you more control over navigation.
  • Taskbar Overflow: Manage multiple open apps and find the window you need quickly with the new taskbar overflow feature.
  • Haptic Sliders: Adds physical-like feedback when adjusting volume or brightness, so changes feel more precise.
  • Adaptive Refresh Rate: Automatically adjusts the screen’s refresh rate based on what you’re doing—high for games, low for reading—to save battery.

In short, both Apple and Google are adding new features. While Apple’s updates feel more noticeable and useful for everyday users, most of them already exist on Android—Apple is simply catching up. Meanwhile, Android 16 introduces more advanced tools, but they’re niche and unlikely to impact the average user. Neither OS offers a feature that significantly changes how you use your phone on a day-to-day basis.

But as mentioned, the major headline change this year on both platforms is design.

Design Spotlight: Liquid Glass vs Material 3 Expressive

Okay, now let’s talk about what actually feels new this year—the look. Both Apple and Google brought their own style to the table.

iOS 26: Liquid Glass

Liquid Glass is Apple’s new design language introduced across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, watchOS 26, and tvOS 26. It gives the interface a dynamic, glass-like appearance with effects that mimic real-world transparency, layering, and reflections.

This design adds depth and motion to everyday UI elements, enhancing their visual appeal. App icons, widgets, buttons, and menus appear as if they are made of layered frosted glass. They reflect the surrounding content and light, adjusting in real time depending on what you’re viewing. Translucent surfaces catch highlights, morph as you scroll or swipe, and transition smoothly between light and dark modes based on context.

Android 16: Material 3 Expressive

Material 3 Expressive is Google’s updated design language built on top of Material You. Google’s design approach is all about color, personalization, and comfort. While Material You concentrated more on bringing wallpaper colors to your UI, Material 3 Expressive gives you and app developers more freedom to experiment with colors.

It brings bold colors, irregular shapes, soft corners, and clear typography. Google is prioritizing layouts that are more fun, unique, and readable.

Material 3 Expressive also emphasizes playful visual feedback. When you dismiss a notification or interact with elements like volume sliders or app previews, the motion feels springy and responsive.

Real Talk: Our Take on the New Designs

Apple’s Liquid Glass looks impressive at first glance, but quickly becomes a distraction. Elements blend too much. Text and icons sometimes lose contrast. It feels a bit too eager to impress and ends up becoming more clumsy. More often than not, I find myself squinting to open an app or adjust any control from the Control Center.

Material 3 Expressive, on the other hand, is still not fully rolled out. Based on what we’ve seen so far and Google’s track record with Material You, the vision sounds more promising than the actual delivery. That said, it leans more toward readability and user comfort, which makes it more promising.

Verdict: Apple went hard on the visuals, but it might be too much. Google is playing it safe, and that might just work better. Preferring one design over another is subjective, but in terms of usability, we believe Google’s design takes the lead, whereas Apple’s Liquid Glass requires some refinement and may need to reduce transparency in certain areas. 

Related: Not a Fan of iOS 26’s Liquid Glass Look? Here’s How to Tone It Down

Final Thoughts: 2025 Is the Year of Form Over Function

If you’re hoping for meaningful new features this year, you might walk away a little disappointed. But if design matters to you, this is the year to pay attention. This will be how both companies move forward with their design style over the next few years.

iOS 26 and Android 16 are both good in their own ways, but this time, the fight isn’t about doing more. It’s about how things look while doing it. That’s why 2025 is clearly the year of form over function.

  • watchOS 26 vs watchOS 11: Is Apple’s Latest Update Really Worth It?
  • macOS Tahoe vs Sequoia: All the Big and Subtle Changes You Need to Know
  • MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

mainEntity.name: Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Is Coming: Launch Set for Late 2026

content.rendered:
After years of speculation and rumors, Apple’s first-ever foldable device, the iPhone Fold, is inching closer to reality. According to the renowned Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, assembly manufacturer Hon Hai (Foxconn) is expected to begin official development of the foldable iPhone project by late Q3 or early Q4 2025.

However, Kuo also notes that Apple has yet to finalize many important components, including the highly anticipated hinge bearings. This highlights Apple’s meticulous approach to hardware engineering as it enters the foldable smartphone segment.

Ming-Chi Kuo shared the update via X (Twitter).

Samsung Display Already Prepping Foldable Panels for Apple

One of the few confirmed components is Samsung’s folding display. Reports suggest that Samsung Display (SDC) has been asked to dedicate a production capacity of 7–8 million foldable panels per year to Apple. While this figure may suggest a large-scale rollout, Kuo clarifies that actual screen shipments in 2026 will be lower due to a limited production window that year.

Foldable iPhone Expected in 2026, Limited Rollout Planned

Recent rumors suggest that Apple has placed an order for 15–20 million foldable iPhones. However, Kuo clarifies that this number refers to total lifecycle shipments spanning 2–3 years, not a single-year shipment volume.

This suggests a cautious rollout, with mass production expected to commence in the second half of 2026. Due to the expected high price tag, yearly sales in 2027 and 2028 are projected to remain in the low millions, placing the device in a niche, premium segment, much like the rollout of the Vision Pro.

All Plans Still Subject to Change

Despite increasing clarity, Kuo says nothing is set in stone. The final design, specifications, and production plans may shift before the project enters mass production.

Foldable iPhone: A Slow but Strategic Rollout

The slow and steady approach that Apple is taking with its foldable iPhone suggests that the Cupertino tech giant is prioritizing hardware perfection over speed to market. However, even with this deliberate approach, we could see a foldable iPhone as early as late 2026, with shipments ramping up gradually over the next few years.

Are you ready to fold? Let us know if you’d consider switching to a foldable iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

mainEntity.name: Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: Facebook Finally Gets Passkey Support on Mobile: What That Means for You

content.rendered:
For a while now, apps like Google, Microsoft, and even WhatsApp have offered passkey logins. Surprisingly, Facebook didn’t—until now. Meta has finally rolled out passkey support for the Facebook mobile app, and it changes how you log in, especially if you’re tired of typing passwords or dealing with two-factor codes.

Passkeys are now live for Facebook on both iOS and Android. If you use Face ID, Touch ID, or a device PIN to unlock your phone, you already have everything you need to use a passkey.

What Is a Passkey and How Does It Work?

A passkey is a modern replacement for your password and 2FA codes. Normally, you have to remember a password and then use a 2FA code to keep the account safe, which makes logging in a hassle. A passkey replaces all of that with your biometrics.

When logging in, simply use your device’s biometrics, such as Face ID, Touch ID, or a PIN, to authenticate. No more typing long passwords or copying SMS codes. Logging in becomes as simple as unlocking your phone.

  • Passkeys can’t be guessed, stolen, or phished.
  • They stay on your device and are never uploaded.
  • They use a technology standard called WebAuthn, backed by the FIDO Alliance (Meta is a member).

Why Passkeys Make Facebook Login More Secure and Convenient

Let’s be honest—passwords are a pain. They’re hard to remember, easy to mess up, and even easier to steal. Passkeys fix all of that. They tie your login to your actual phone. That means someone across the world can’t just trick you with a fake link and steal your password—they’d need your phone in their hand to even try.

Plus, your browser or app will only trigger a passkey login if it’s the real Facebook domain. So phishing pages won’t even get that far.

Which Devices Support Facebook Passkeys?

Right now, passkey support is limited to mobile devices, and here’s how it plays out:

  • Facebook App on Android and iOS: Passkeys are rolling out, so if you’re using the app on your phone, you’ll soon be able to log in with just your fingerprint, face, or PIN. No password needed.
  • Messenger App: Support isn’t live yet, but Meta has confirmed it’s coming soon. Once enabled, you won’t need to create a separate passkey—Messenger will use the same one you set up for Facebook.
  • Desktop Browsers: These still rely on your password or other traditional login methods. Passkeys don’t work on desktops yet, so you’ll have to wait a bit longer for a full passwordless experience across all devices.

How to Set Up Facebook Passkey Login on Your Phone

Setting up a passkey is extremely easy and takes only a minute.

  1. Open the Facebook app on your phone.
  2. Open the Menu tab.
  3. Select the Settings & privacy option and then tap Settings.
  4. Under Account Center, tap See more in Account Center
  5. Tap Password and Security > Passkey.
  6. Tap the Create Passkey and follow on-device instructions.

You might also see a prompt to create a passkey the next time you log in.

To use passkeys, make sure you’re running the latest version of the Facebook app on your mobile device. While Meta hasn’t officially mentioned a specific version number, these features usually roll out through app updates in phases. So, if you don’t see the passkey option in your settings, make sure to update your Facebook app from the App Store or Google Play Store.

Most modern smartphones come equipped with biometric features, such as fingerprint scanners, face recognition, or secure PIN locks, which are necessary for using passkeys. However, if your phone is older or lacks these features and doesn’t support passkeys, don’t worry—you can still log in using your password and two-factor authentication or security keys, just like before.

What Else Can You Do with a Facebook Passkey?

Passkeys aren’t just for logging in. Meta is building more features around them to make your online life both simpler and more secure.

  • Meta Pay: When shopping online through Facebook, you can use your passkey to securely autofill your payment information, eliminating the need for manual card entry.
  • Encrypted Backups on Messenger: Once Messenger gets passkey support, it’ll also extend to protecting your end-to-end encrypted message backups. This adds an extra layer of privacy, making sure only you can access your backup data.

Why Facebook Passkeys Are a Game-Changer for Mobile Security

This update finally brings Facebook in line with other major platforms that already support passkeys. It’s safer, faster, and easier. If you hate remembering passwords or dealing with phishing risks, this is the upgrade you’ve been waiting for.

Additionally, with Messenger and Meta Pay also joining the party, it’s clear that Meta is making a significant investment in passkeys.

Give it a try next time you log in—you might never want to type your Facebook password again.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

mainEntity.name: Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: Craig Federighi on Why Apple Refuses to Turn the iPad Into a Mac

content.rendered:
With every new iPad Pro release and major iPadOS update, one question keeps popping up: Why can’t the iPad just run macOS? After all, the latest iPads are powered by the same M-series chips used in MacBooks. And with iPadOS 26 now bringing full-blown windowing and desktop-like multitasking, the line between iPad and Mac feels blurrier than ever.

But Apple says: no. Not now, not ever. And they’ve got a very specific reason.

Craig Federighi Explains the “Spork” Philosophy

In a recent interview at MacStories, Apple’s software chief Craig Federighi said Apple doesn’t want to build a spork.

“If a spoon’s great and a fork’s great, let’s combine them, right? But you end up with something that’s not a good spoon or a good fork.”

To Apple, merging macOS and iPadOS into a single device would make both worse. That’s why iPad will never just turn into a Mac — even if it keeps borrowing ideas from one.

iPadOS 26: A Giant Leap, Still Not macOS

This year, iPadOS 26 brings the biggest changes to iPad multitasking yet:

  • A brand-new windowing engine replaces the old Stage Manager system.
  • The OS now uses smart-prioritization engine to keep up to 12 apps active, especially on M4 iPads.
  • iPad apps now include three buttons at the top left — close, minimize, and maximize — just like on a Mac.
  • Menu options are also now available at the top of the screen. 

Despite all this, Apple is careful not to compromise on what makes the iPad special: its simplicity and touch-first interface.

According to Federighi, Apple sees two types of iPad users:

  1. People who want a simple, immersive experience — one app, full screen.
  2. Power users who want more control—multiple windows, multitasking, keyboard, and Pencil support.

iPadOS 26 is Apple’s way of serving both, without turning the iPad into a Mac.

Why Apple Won’t Let iPad Run macOS

Federighi didn’t dodge the question. He explained that merging the Mac and iPad would compromise the strengths of each.

“The Mac lets the iPad be iPad.”

Apple wants consistency where it makes sense — like shared app frameworks — but every device still needs its own soul. macOS is for precision, flexibility, and legacy software. iPadOS is for touch, Pencil, and ease of use.

Running both OSes on one device might sound like the best of both worlds. But Apple sees that as messy, confusing, and against their design philosophy.

The Real-World Debate

Online, opinions are all over the place.

Some folks cheer Apple’s stance — they’ve seen what happened with the Surface Pro and call it a half-baked compromise. To them, the Mac is for serious work, and the iPad is its own thing — lightweight, simple, and a touch-first operating system.

Others aren’t buying it. They argue that iPadOS, with its app support, is limited by its software, especially with all that power packed into the M4 iPad Pro. Some users are at least asking for the option to switch to macOS when needed. If Macs can run Windows in a virtual machine, why can’t iPads do the same for macOS?

Even within the team at iGeeks Media, opinions are divided.

At the end of the day, Apple is betting that keeping the iPad and Mac separate — while letting them learn from each other — is the right path forward. The iPad can become more powerful, but not at the cost of its identity.

So no, your iPad won’t run macOS. But if you look closely, you’ll realize it doesn’t need to. It’s already carving out its own space — just don’t call it a spork.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay online?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

mainEntity.name: Why do some major stores not accept Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: Workout Buddy in watchOS 26: Meet Your AI Fitness Coach on the Wrist

content.rendered:
Apple’s watchOS 26 keynote may not have been packed with groundbreaking announcements, but one standout feature did capture our attention—Workout Buddy. Powered by Apple Intelligence, it transforms your Apple Watch into an AI-enabled fitness coach that provides voice feedback to keep you focused and inspired throughout your workouts.

If you’re curious about how Workout Buddy works and how to set it up, this guide has everything you need to get started.

What is Workout Buddy in watchOS 26?

Workout Buddy is a new AI-powered feature baked into the Workout app in watchOS 26. It uses Apple Intelligence to analyze a combination of real-time workout data, your history, Activity Ring progress, pace, training load, and more, then delivers motivational voice feedback during your session.

Here’s everything Workout Buddy can do:

  • Gives you a motivational boost at the start of your workout.
  • Provides real-time spoken updates on your performance (distance, pace, heart rate, milestones).
  • Delivers a customized spoken summary at the end of your session.

Apple has developed a new text-to-speech engine trained using the voices of real Apple Fitness+ trainers. The result? A voice that sounds more like your upbeat gym coach than a robotic assistant—personalized and energetic.

Requirements to Use Workout Buddy on Apple Watch

Before you get started, make sure you meet these conditions:

  • A watchOS 26-compatible Apple Watch (available on Apple Watch Series 6 or later).
  • As Workout Buddy is an Apple Intelligence-powered feature, the paired iPhone must be an iPhone 15 Pro or newer model with iOS 26 installed.
  • Bluetooth headphones connected to your Apple Watch or iPhone to ensure you hear the audio feedback clearly during workouts.
  • English language setting, as it’s currently the only supported language at launch.

How to Set Up Workout Buddy on Apple Watch

Before you start using Workout Buddy on your Apple Watch, you must first set it up:

  1. Open the Workout app on your Apple Watch.
  2. Select a supported workout: Running, Walking, Cycling, or Strength Training.
  3. Tap the Alerts icon in the top-left corner.
  4. Scroll and tap on Workout Buddy.
  5. Toggle the switch to Enable Workout Buddy.


  6. Connect your AirPods or Bluetooth earbuds to your Apple Watch or iPhone.

How to Use Workout Buddy During a Workout

Once everything’s set up, you don’t need to do anything, as Workout Buddy activates automatically as you start the workout. Here’s how it works:

  • In the Workout app, select the workout you enabled Workout Buddy in and hit the Play (Start) button to begin your workout.
  • Workout Buddy kicks in immediately with a motivational phrase like, “Let’s crush that 5K today!”
  • During the session, it shares spoken updates on distance, pace, heart rate, and other milestones.
  • At the end, you’ll get a custom audio recap—“You ran 3.5 miles at an 8:20 pace. Great job beating last week!”

Everything is processed on-device, ensuring your privacy while also allowing it to work offline—no internet connection is needed.

Customizing Workout Buddy to Match Your Style

Apple already knew that not all users may be thrilled about the prospect of having an AI cheerleader during a challenging run or other training sessions. Additionally, while some users may prefer the default AI voice, some may not. That’s why Apple hasn’t made Workout Buddy a one-size-fits-all feature. Here are some ways to make it work for you:

  • Workout Buddy isn’t an opt-out feature; instead, it’s an opt-in. Thus, you can turn it on for certain workouts and keep it disabled for others if you prefer silence.
  • Adjust the voice style: Similar to Siri, Workout Buddy offers you multiple voice styles you can choose from. To do so, open the Workout app → Select a supported workout → Tap Alerts → Workout Buddy → Choose Voice Style.

  • Customize the on-screen data in your Workout app alongside the voice coaching. To do so, open the Workout app → Select a supported workout → Tap Workout Views → Tap the Edit button at top right corner of the Workout View and make the desired changes.

Workout Buddy Not Responding on Apple Watch? Try These Fixes

If Workout Buddy isn’t working as expected—or not at all—try these troubleshooting tips:

  1. Check Device Compatibility: Check whether your Apple Watch supports watchOS 26 and runs it. Additionally, the paired iPhone is an iPhone 15 Pro or newer model with iOS 26 installed.
  2. Connect Bluetooth Headphones: Workout Buddy only works when AirPods or other Bluetooth earbuds are connected to your Apple Watch or iPhone. Press the Side button to open the Control Center → tap the AirPlay icon → ensure your headphones are selected.
  3. Keep iPhone Nearby: Workout Buddy requires Apple Intelligence processing to work. Since Apple Intelligence isn’t available natively on the Apple Watch, the paired iPhone must be within Bluetooth range during the workout.
  4. Enable Workout Buddy: The Workout Buddy feature in watchOS 26 isn’t enabled by default. Therefore, ensure that you have enabled it for the supported workout in the Workout app.
  5. Choose a Supported Workout: Workout Buddy doesn’t work with all activities. Supported types include Outdoor/Indoor Run, Walk, Cycling, HIIT, Strength Training. If you’re doing something unsupported (such as Yoga, Dance, or Mindfulness) or (such as yoga, dance, or mindfulness), you won’t find the option to enable it.
  6. Check Audio Volume: Ensure your AirPods or Bluetooth headphones aren’t muted.
  7. Restart Both Devices: If nothing works, there might be a bug affecting the functionality. Restarting your devices often eliminates such bugs and glitches.

No More Boring Workouts…

At first glance, Workout Buddy might seem like just another gimmick. But once you try it, you’ll realize it’s a powerful step toward personalized fitness. Whether you need a motivational nudge or real-time coaching, this AI fitness companion can help you push through that final mile or rep.

Are you excited to try Workout Buddy on watchOS 26? Share your thoughts or questions in the comments—we’d love to hear how it works for you.

title.rendered: Here’s Why Apple Skipped iOS 19 and Jumped Straight to iOS 26

content.rendered:
When the entire tech world was anticipating the launch of iOS 19, Apple pulled an unexpected move—playing what felt like a digital UNO Skip card—and branded its next big iPhone update as iOS 26. No iOS 19, 20, 21—or even 25. Just 26.

While the WWDC 2025 keynote spotlighted the stunning Liquid Glass UI and powerful Apple Intelligence features, the internet buzzed with one big question: What happened to iOS 19?

Even now, with WWDC wrapped, many are still wondering: Why did Apple make this radical version jump? Let’s break it down.

1. Year-Based Naming Strategy

Apple appears to be following a new trend seen in the auto industry: naming the product after the year it’s meant to be used in.

Since iOS 26 will serve as the primary operating system throughout 2026, Apple chose to align the version number accordingly—even though the update rolls out in September 2025.

In short, Apple is moving towards calendar-aligned OS versions, starting with iOS.

2. Unified Versioning Across All Apple Platforms

Before WWDC 2025, Apple’s operating systems followed inconsistent versioning:

  • iOS was on 18
  • iPadOS and tvOS were on 18
  • macOS was at 15
  • watchOS was at 11
  • visionOS was at 2

This inconsistency often created confusion for users, developers, and marketers alike. However, with WWDC 2025, Apple synchronized every OS to version 26:

  • iOS 26
  • iPadOS 26
  • macOS 26
  • watchOS 26
  • tvOS 26
  • visionOS 26

This unified versioning system simplifies product documentation, cross-platform feature rollout, and marketing messaging. As Apple devices become more integrated, consistency becomes key.

3. It Signals a Major Leap—Not Just an Increment

This isn’t your average annual update. iOS 26 represents one of the most significant transformations of the iPhone experience since iOS 7.

Key highlights of iOS 26:

  • Liquid Glass design: The first major visual overhaul in a decade.
  • Apple Intelligence: An enhanced AI-powered system integrated throughout the OS.
  • On-screen Visual Intelligence: You can now analyze what’s on your screen and interact with text, images, and context in real time.
  • Live call translation and smart call screening.
  • ChatGPT system integration across apps and system-level actions.

In short, iOS 26 marks the start of a whole new era for iPhones. A version number like iOS 19 wouldn’t have captured the magnitude of this shift.

Related: How to Use Live Translation in iOS 26 for Calls, FaceTime, and Messages

4. The AI Era Begins: Apple Intelligence 2.0

While Apple Intelligence debuted in iOS 18, many features were rolled out slowly and received criticism for lacking depth or practicality.

Apple listened. With iOS 26, Apple Intelligence is no longer a novelty—it’s central to the entire user experience.

Here’s what it brings:

  • Summarizing notifications and web pages
  • Suggesting context-aware replies for messages and emails
  • Enhancing image editing and search
  • Powering a smarter, more intuitive Siri
  • Smarter Shortcuts with Intelligent Actions

This is Apple’s AI era, and iOS 26 is its foundation. Skipping to iOS 26 emphasizes that this isn’t a typical update—it’s a leap into the future.

Related: Apple Intelligence Features Unveiled at WWDC 2025

A Bold Version Number for a Bold Release

So, why did Apple skip iOS 19 and jump straight to iOS 26?

Because iOS 26 is more than just a software update—it represents a new design philosophy, a unified Apple ecosystem, and a future powered by real-time intelligence and machine learning.

This move isn’t cosmetic—it’s strategic, symbolic, and practical. And it sets the tone for Apple’s OS lineup moving forward.

Do you think Apple made the right move by skipping iOS 19 and rebranding it as iOS 26? We’d love to hear your thoughts.

  • iOS 26 vs iOS 18: Big Changes You’ll Notice Right Away
  • iOS 26 CarPlay Features That Will Make You Want to Drive More

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

title.rendered: watchOS 26 vs watchOS 11: Is Apple’s Latest Update Really Worth It?

content.rendered:
With every new watchOS release, Apple raises the bar for smartwatch personalization and intelligence. While watchOS 11 focused on smarter health tracking and performance metrics, watchOS 26 redefines the Apple Watch experience with a visually stunning interface and integrated Apple Intelligence features.

Let’s break down how watchOS 26 compares to watchOS 11 so you can decide whether the upgrade is worth your time and your wrist.

What’s New in watchOS 26 Compared to watchOS 11?

Here’s a quick feature comparison before we dive deeper:

watchOS 26 introduces a wave of enhancements over watchOS 11, featuring a sleek new interface and a more personalized, interactive, and intelligent Apple Watch experience.

1. Redesigned Interface with Liquid Glass Animations

Taking cues from iOS 26, watchOS 26 introduces a Liquid Glass UI that transforms the way you interact with your Apple Watch. The new interface brings in-depth, blur effects, and system-wide fluid transitions, making everything feel more immersive—just like on your iPhone or Mac.

2. Apple Intelligence Comes to Apple Watch

Apple Intelligence, which debuted on iPhone with iOS 18, now makes its way to the Apple Watch. While features like Visual Intelligence and Writing Tools are still iPhone-exclusive, watchOS 26 offers the following AI-powered tools:

  • Workout Buddy: Virtual fitness coach with real-time guidance.
  • Smarter Replies: AI-suggested messages in the Messages app.
  • Live Call Translation: Supports real-time translation when paired with an iPhone 15 Pro or newer.

Note: You’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or later to unlock Apple Intelligence features on your Apple Watch.

3. Smart Stack Just Got Smarter

watchOS 11 brought Live Activities to the Apple Watch, but watchOS 26 takes Smart Stack to the next level. It now uses contextual awareness to surface the right widgets at the right time.

For example, if you’re in a new location with no signal, your watch will automatically show a Backtrack widget to help you navigate back safely.

4. Notes App Debuts on Apple Watch

As mentioned, with watchOS 11, Apple primarily focused on fitness and related features, which is why we received the Vitals app. However, in watchOS 26, along with the fitness-centric features, Apple kept productivity in mind. Thus, for the first time, watchOS 26 brings the Notes app to your wrist. You can use the Notes app on the Apple Watch to:

  • View and edit existing notes.
  • Dictate new ones using Siri.
  • Check off items in to-do lists.
  • Pin important notes for quick access.

5. Upgraded Workout and Health Experience

While watchOS 11 introduced powerful tools like the Vitals app and Training Load to help users understand their recovery and exertion levels, watchOS 26 takes fitness coaching to the next level, thanks to the all-new Workout Buddy.

Using the power of Apple Intelligence, Workout Buddy functions as a virtual fitness assistant, providing you with real-time feedback, motivation, and insightful guidance during your workouts. Whether you’re running, cycling, or doing strength training, Workout Buddy can:

  • Offer real-time voice coaching based on your pace and heart rate
  • Celebrate milestones as you hit goals.
  • Suggest adjustments if you’re overtraining or underperforming.
  • Summarize performance at the end of each workout.

Other workout and health upgrades in watchOS 26 include:

  • A redesigned Workout app with a cleaner layout and easier access to controls.
  • Automatic music playback for curated or recent playlists when you begin a workout.
  • Personalized workout suggestions based on your trends and schedule.

Who Should Upgrade to watchOS 26?

While watchOS 26 has many compelling reasons to upgrade, it may not be for everyone; you must fall into one of the following groups:

  • Own a watchOS 26 compatible Apple Watch model (Apple Watch Series 6 and newer models).
  • You are a fitness-focused individual who wants to benefit from smarter coaching (Fitness Buddy) and better goal tracking.
  • You own an iPhone 15 Pro or newer model.
  • If you are using iOS 26 on the paired iPhone, you cannot pair an Apple Watch running watchOS 11 with the iPhone running iOS 26.

Release Timeline and Compatibility

Pros and Cons of watchOS 26

Every operating system, regardless of its quality, has its pros and cons, and the same is true for watchOS 26. Have a look at the below-listed pros and cons to make your decision:

Pros

  • Sleek Liquid Glass UI and fluid animations.
  • AI-powered features and coaching.
  • Built-in Notes app for productivity.
  • Smart Stack improvements.
  • More interactive gestures and suggestions.

Cons

  • Apple Intelligence requires newer iPhones.
  • Some features (like wrist flick) only work on newer Apple Watch models.
  • watchOS 26 is still in beta and may have early bugs.

How to Upgrade to watchOS 26 from watchOS 11

Here’s how you can install the watchOS 26 developer beta on your Apple Watch using your iPhone running iOS 26. Here’s how:

  1. Open Watch app → General → Software Update.
  2. If the watchOS 26 update is available, hit Download and Install.
  3. If you want to install iOS 26 beta, tap Beta Updates and select the appropriate watchOS 26 beta option.

Final Verdict: Is watchOS 26 Worth the Upgrade?

If you own a newer Apple Watch and iPhone 15 Pro or above, watchOS 26 is absolutely worth it. With a refreshing UI, smarter workout tools, the new Notes app, and Apple Intelligence features, it transforms your Apple Watch into a more dynamic personal assistant.

However, if you’re using an older device or aren’t upgrading your iPhone, you might want to hold off until all features are fully supported on your hardware.

Tell us—are you upgrading to watchOS 26 or sticking with watchOS 11? Drop your thoughts in the comments!

title.rendered: Ads Are Now Live on WhatsApp: What You Need to Know

content.rendered:
After years of resistance, WhatsApp is officially no longer ad-free. Meta has confirmed that advertisements are rolling out on the platform, marking a major shift in how users interact with the world’s most popular messaging app. The update, quietly detailed on Meta’s official WhatsApp blog, introduces two ad formats—bringing the app more in line with Instagram and Facebook.

Where You’ll See WhatsApp Ads

WhatsApp won’t interrupt your private or group chats with ads—at least not yet. Instead, Meta is taking a more calculated approach:

  • Status Ads: These will appear in the Status section (similar to Instagram Stories), where users already post temporary photo and video updates.
  • Sponsored Channels: WhatsApp Channels, which let you follow content from creators or organizations, will now include promoted channels clearly labeled as “Sponsored.”

This means you’ll only see ads in parts of the app where content is already public or semi-public.

Related: How to Use WhatsApp Channels on iPhone

What These Ads Will Look Like

If you’re familiar with Meta’s other platforms, you already know what to expect.

  • Status Ads will be full-screen, visually rich, and interactive, allowing users to swipe up for more.
  • Sponsored Channels will blend into the Channels feed but will carry a “sponsored” tag to differentiate from organic content.

The goal is seamless integration—ads that look like they belong, yet stand out just enough for transparency.

How Private Are These Ads, Really?

Meta claims this rollout is being done “in the most private way possible.” That’s a big promise—especially when personalization is involved.

Here’s what Meta may use to target ads:

  • Your country or city
  • Your language
  • The Channels you follow
  • Your interactions with the ads you see

If you’ve linked your WhatsApp with Meta’s Account Center, ad preferences from your Facebook and Instagram activity will also inform what you see in WhatsApp.

Recommended: How to Use WhatsApp Privacy Checkup on iPhone

Why This Change Matters

Let’s be clear: this is a huge moment for WhatsApp.

The app has long stood as one of the last ad-free holdouts in Meta’s portfolio. With this shift, even the most privacy-conscious users must now deal with marketing in their messaging experience.

For now, Meta is limiting ads to public sections—but history tells us this may not be the end. We’ve seen similar “slow rollouts” on Instagram and Facebook that eventually evolved into broader ad ecosystems.

iGeeksBlog’s Take

We believe this is just the beginning. While Meta assures us that private chats will remain untouched, ads creeping into Status and Channels could open the door for more aggressive placements in the future. The monetization of WhatsApp has always been inevitable, but it’s still jarring to see it finally arrive.

Yes, WhatsApp remains end-to-end encrypted, but that no longer means ad-free.

Are you okay with ads in WhatsApp? Let us know in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

mainEntity.name: Can I use Apple Pay at small businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

title.rendered: macOS 26 Tahoe Brings Phone App to Mac: How to Use It and Why It Matters

content.rendered:
Apple’s latest update, macOS 26 Tahoe, introduces a long-awaited feature—an official Phone app on Mac. For the first time, you can make and receive calls, manage voicemails, and access advanced calling features directly from your Mac. Thanks to Apple’s Continuity enhancements, the iPhone experience is now fully integrated with your desktop setup.

Sounds interesting, right? In this article, I’ll share everything you need to know about the Phone app on macOS 26, from its key features to how to use it, along with troubleshooting tips.   

iOS Calling Experience Now on Mac

The new Phone app in macOS 26 marks a huge upgrade to Apple’s Continuity ecosystem. Until now, you could only take calls on your Mac via FaceTime. But with the dedicated Phone app, you get a full-blown iOS-like calling experience that feels native and seamless.

With Continuity, your Mac syncs with your iPhone’s calls, contacts, and voicemails. That means you can place or receive calls directly from your Mac—no need to touch your iPhone. As someone who spends hours on a Mac daily, this change is a major productivity boost.

The interface mirrors the iPhone’s Phone app layout, featuring tabs for Favorites, Recents, Contacts, and Voicemails. It feels like your Mac just became your second phone.

Requirements to Use the Phone App on Mac

To use the Phone app on macOS 26, make sure you meet these requirements:

  • Mac running macOS 26 (Apple Silicon: M1 or newer).
  • iPhone running iOS 26 with an active cellular plan.
  • Same Apple ID signed in on both iPhone and Mac, including FaceTime.
  • Continuity features, including Handoff, must be enabled on both devices. Go to Settings > General > AirDrop & Handoff. 

  • Your Mac and iPhone must be connected via the same Wi-Fi network. They should be within 30 feet of each other for reliable performance.  
  • Calls on Other Devices enabled: On iPhone, go to Settings > Phone > Calls on Other Devices and enable it. Then, on Mac, go to Phone > Settings > Calls and turn on Calls from iPhone.

  • Apple Intelligence features, such as Live Translation, require an M1 or later Mac and an iPhone 15 Pro or newer.
  • An external microphone or headset is required for Mac mini, Mac Studio, and Mac Pro.

Top Features of the Phone App on macOS 26

Apple packed several powerful calling tools into the macOS Phone app. Here are the key features:

  • Call Screening: Apple Intelligence automatically answers calls from unknown numbers, identifies the caller, and lets you decide whether to accept or send to voicemail.

  • Hold Assist: Hate waiting on hold? Your Mac can now detect hold music, stay on the line, and notify you when a real person answers.

  • Live Translation: During a call, it provides real-time audio translations, so you and the caller hear AI-generated translations in your preferred languages. It supports languages like English, French, German, Portuguese, and Spanish. 

  • Live Activities Integration: Active call status appears in your Mac’s menu bar, just like timers or rideshare updates.

All of this is wrapped in macOS 26’s sleek new Liquid Glass design, giving the Phone app a polished, modern feel.

How to Use the Phone App on Mac

Here’s how to get started:

Dialing a Contact 

  1. Launch the Phone app on your Mac (it’s pre-installed with macOS 26). For first-time users, sign in with your Apple Account.

     
  2. In the app’s unified interface,  
    • Click a contact under the Favorites tab to call them.

       
    • Use the Keypad button to enter a phone number manually.

    • Type a contact name in the Search bar and click the call icon.  
  3. Click the call button to start the call. Your Mac uses your iPhone’s cellular connection via Continuity, so no cellular plan on the Mac is needed. 
  4. Use your Mac’s microphone and speakers or connect AirPods for better audio quality. 

Receive Calls

  1. When a call comes in, a pop-up appears in the top-right corner of your Mac’s screen, showing the caller’s name or number (and their Contact Poster, if set). 

  2. Click Answer to accept the call, or Decline to send it to voicemail.

  3. If Call Screening is enabled, unknown callers will be prompted to identify themselves, and you’ll see their response before deciding to answer. 

During the call, you can click the mic icon to mute yourself.

View Call History

  1. Open the Phone app and scroll down to see the Recents section. 
  2. You’ll see a list of recent calls synced from your iPhone, including missed, answered, and outgoing calls.

  3. Click a call to view details or return the call with one click. You can also view all the calls with that contact by clicking Call History. 

To delete a call log, click Edit at the top > Select. Now, choose the call log and click Delete at the bottom. 

 

Set a Contact Poster

By default, your iPhone’s Contact Posters sync to Mac. You can customize it from your Contacts app on Mac. For other contacts, you may add custom photos as Contact Posters. 

  1. In the Phone app, select a contact. 
  2. Click the dropdown icon next to Contact Photo & Poster and select Custom Photo. 

     

You can edit contact details by clicking the Edit button at the top right corner and selecting Edit Contact Info. 

Note

This feature was found to be unstable during testing in the macOS 26 Developer Beta.

Record a Call

  1. During a call, look for the Record button in the Phone app’s interface. 
  2. Click to start recording. The call is saved securely on your Mac and can be transcribed using Apple Intelligence. 
  3. Access recordings in the Notes app, where you can export or share them. This feature also works on iPhone and iPad. 

Check Voicemails 

  1. In the Phone app, tap the menu icon (three-line icon) at the top and select Voicemails.

     
  2. Under the Voicemails tab, you will see a list of voicemails that were synced from your iPhone. 
  3. Click a voicemail to listen to it or see its transcription. You can also add the caller to your contacts or report it as spam.

     

macOS 26 Tahoe also supports Live Voicemail that shows real-time transcriptions as the caller leaves a message, so you can decide whether to pick up mid-message. 

Block or Unblock a Number

To block a contact, click their call from Recents on the left side. It will show the call details. Scroll down and select Block Contact. Confirm your choice by clicking Block Contact on the popup. 

You can also unblock numbers on your Phone app on Mac.

  1. Click Phone at the top menu bar and select Settings.

     
  2. Move to the Blocked tab and click the number you want to unblock. 
  3. Click the minus (–) icon at the bottom to remove the number.

      

These steps make the Phone app intuitive, whether you’re managing calls or voicemails. The app’s design ensures everything is accessible in one place, so you don’t need to switch between tabs constantly. 

Limitations to Keep in Mind

While the Phone app is a major upgrade, there are some limitations to keep in mind: 

  • iPhone Dependency: The Phone app relies on Continuity, meaning you need an iPhone nearby with an active cellular plan. Also, some features need Apple Intelligence to be enabled on the iPhone. 
  • Language Support: Several features, such as Call Screening and Live Translation, are currently limited to English, French, German, Portuguese, and Spanish for Phone and FaceTime calls.  
  • Continuity Bugs: Some users report occasional glitches with Continuity, especially when multiple Apple ID accounts are logged into the same Mac.  
  • Hardware Requirements: The Phone app requires macOS 26, which only supports M1 or newer Macs, leaving older Intel-based models out. 

Phone App Not Working on macOS 26? Try These Quick Fixes

You may run into errors like “iPhone Calls Not Available on” on your Mac while dialing a number.

If the Phone app isn’t working as expected on your Mac, try these troubleshooting steps: 

  1. Check Compatibility: Ensure your Mac supports macOS 26 (M1 or newer). If not, the Phone app won’t be available. 
  2. Check Continuity Settings: Ensure your iPhone and Mac are signed into the same Apple ID, and Wi-Fi is enabled. Go to System Settings > General > AirDrop & Handoff on your Mac and enable Handoff. 
  3. Update Devices: Ensure your Mac is running macOS 26 and your iPhone is on iOS 26. Check for updates in Settings > General > Software Update. 
  4. Restart Devices: A quick restart of your Mac and iPhone can fix connectivity issues. 
  5. Reset Network Settings: On your iPhone, go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Network Settings. Note that this clears Wi-Fi passwords. 

If issues persist, contact Apple Support for expert advice. 

Will Macs Ever Go Cellular?

With this new Phone app, rumors are buzzing around cellular-capable Macs. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is exploring adding a modem chip to future Macs, possibly by 2026. This would bring native calling and texting—no iPhone needed.

But for now, Apple is clearly doubling down on Continuity. And with the new Phone app, it’s working better than ever.

Stay Connected with macOS 26’s Phone App

The new Phone app in macOS 26 is more than just a utility—it’s a major step forward for Apple’s ecosystem. With native call controls, voicemail access, real-time translation, and call recording all in one place, your Mac just became smarter and more useful.

Whether you’re a remote worker, a multitasker, or just someone who hates picking up their phone, this feature is one you’ll love using.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • macOS Tahoe vs Sequoia: All the Big and Subtle Changes You Need to Know
  • How to Use and Customize Control Center on Mac (macOS 26 Included)
  • Apple’s New Games App: Everything You Need to Know

mainEntity.name: Can someone see how many times you view their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any app or service claiming to reveal your Instagram profile viewers is misleading and potentially dangerous.

mainEntity.name: Can someone see if you viewed their Instagram profile picture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Viewing someone's profile picture does not trigger any notification, and there is no way for users to see who has viewed their profile photo.

mainEntity.name: Can you see who viewed your Instagram Highlights?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Highlights are made up of Stories, but once a Story becomes a Highlight, you can no longer see who viewed it.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many websites and apps now accept Apple Pay as a payment option.

mainEntity.name: Which browsers support Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay works in Safari on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a store accepts Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.

mainEntity.name: Are there fees for using Apple Pay?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, Apple Pay does not charge users any fees.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes! Many small and independent merchants now accept Apple Pay. If you see the contactless symbol at checkout, you can use Apple Pay.

acceptedAnswer.text: Some retailers have chosen to develop their own mobile payment systems, or have not upgraded their payment terminals to support NFC. Others may have business reasons for not supporting Apple Pay.

title.rendered: iOS 26 Finally Lets You Transfer eSIM to Android — Here’s How

content.rendered:
With iOS 26, Apple has quietly broken a long-standing wall that limited users’ freedom to switch platforms. You can now transfer your eSIM from an iPhone to an Android device—and vice versa—without needing to call your carrier. This subtle but powerful update marks a huge leap toward platform flexibility, especially for those ready to make the jump from iOS to Android (or back again).

iPhone to Android eSIM Transfers: Now Much Easier

Thanks to a discovery by a Reddit user on US Mobile’s Dark Star eSIM, a new “Transfer to Android” option has appeared in the Cellular settings on iPhones running iOS 26 beta. This new setting lets users migrate their eSIM profiles directly to Android—no carrier calls, no waiting for a new QR code.

It’s a small toggle with massive implications, cutting down a traditionally clunky, manual process into a near-seamless experience.

However, the feature is still in its early stages. It may not work with all carriers or plans just yet, so it’s worth waiting for the stable iOS 26 rollout before relying on it.

Moving to iPhone? Android to iOS Just Got Easier Too

iOS 26 also includes a new “Transfer from Android” option when setting up a new eSIM on iPhone. Tapping it generates a QR code your Android device can scan, starting the transfer. This method also works in reverse: Android generates a QR code, and your iPhone scans it.

This looks like a coordinated effort between Apple and Google, as the Android 16 beta also hinted at native cross-platform eSIM support.

Why This Update Matters

While iPhone-to-iPhone eSIM transfers have been smooth since iOS 18, switching between iPhone and Android was a hassle and required:

  • Reaching out to your carrier
  • Waiting for a QR code
  • Manually deleting and activating eSIM profiles

With iOS 26, that’s no longer the case.

Cross-platform eSIM transfers are now easier, faster, and more user-controlled, empowering people to change ecosystems without getting stuck in technical red tape.

Switching Made Simple

Whether you’re moving to Android for customization freedom or jumping to iPhone for iOS 26 features like Apple Intelligence or Call Recording, this change ensures your carrier doesn’t slow you down.

Apple appears to be moving toward a more platform-agnostic future—something users have long been asking for.

What do you think about Apple and Google finally working together on this? Could this pave the way for easier data transfers in the future? Let us know in the comments!

acceptedAnswer.text: No—Instagram never shares this information. You can visit any profile as often as you want without the other person knowing.

mainEntity.name: Can business or creator accounts see who viewed their profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Professional accounts can only see the total number of profile visits and general demographic data—not specific visitors.

mainEntity.name: Are there any legitimate apps to check profile viewers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout, or check in Apple Maps.
